austria.h: What the Austrian Ministry of Finance adds
p: The Austrian Ministry of Finance (BMF) applies the tobacco allowance only to travellers aged 17 or over, and says it can be split proportionally between products. Heated tobacco is handled differently: tobacco sticks are not part of the cigarette allowance but fall under the general value limit, and within it you may bring at most 800 sticks, or 250 g if they are packed another way.

That value limit is EUR 430 for air travellers and EUR 300 for everyone else, and EUR 150 for travellers under 15. Above the guideline quantities you must be able to show the tobacco is for your own use, and anything over the allowance, or not for personal use, needs a customs declaration. If you enter through another EU country, that country's rules may differ.
austria.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Austrian Ministry of Finance, Freimengen und Freigrenze (bmf.gv.at). The page carries no date.
faq: Do heated tobacco sticks count as cigarettes in Austria?
No. The Austrian Ministry of Finance puts tobacco sticks under the general value limit instead, and within it allows at most 800 sticks, or 250 g if packed another way.
What is the value limit for other goods entering Austria?
EUR 430 for air travellers and EUR 300 for everyone else, and EUR 150 for travellers under 15, according to the Austrian Ministry of Finance.

p: Czech Customs, on a page published on 13 May 2025, goes further than the EU summary: besides the classic 200 cigarettes (or 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco) it sets separate limits for newer products. You may bring 100 g of refills for heated tobacco, 100 g of other tobacco products, 20 ml of e-cigarette refills, 100 g of nicotine pouches and 100 g of other nicotine products.

The categories can be combined as long as their percentages add up to no more than 100% of the allowance. The tobacco exemption does not apply to travellers under 17, and tobacco is not counted toward the EUR 430 air-travel value limit.
czechia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Czech Customs Administration, information for travellers from third countries (celnisprava.gov.cz), published 13 May 2025.
faq: What are the Czech limits for e-cigarette liquid and nicotine pouches?
Czech Customs allows 20 ml of e-cigarette refills, 100 g of nicotine pouches and 100 g of heated tobacco refills, on a page published on 13 May 2025.
Is tobacco counted in the Czech value limit?
No. Czech Customs says tobacco and alcohol do not count toward the EUR 430 air-travel value limit.

p: The Croatian Customs Administration separates arrivals by transport: from a third country by air or sea you may bring 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco, while by road, rail or other transport the limit is 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g. It also lists newer products: 50 g of heated tobacco, 10 ml of e-liquid and 50 g of new tobacco products.

For goods already bought in the EU with duty paid, travellers over 17 may carry up to 800 cigarettes, 400 cigarillos, 200 cigars or 1 kg of smoking tobacco. Quantities above those must be returned abroad, and undeclared excess is detained until the offence is processed. Border residents and transport staff have lower daily limits, for example 25 cigarettes.
croatia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Croatian Customs Administration, relief from duties for passengers (carina.gov.hr). The page shows no update date.
faq: How does the Croatian tobacco allowance change by transport?
By air or sea you may bring 200 cigarettes; by road, rail or other transport the limit is 40 cigarettes, says Croatian Customs.
What are the Croatian limits for heated tobacco and e-liquid?
Croatian Customs lists 50 g of heated tobacco, 10 ml of e-liquid and 50 g of new tobacco products.

p: The Cyprus Customs and Excise Department says tobacco relief is 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos (max 3 g each), 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco, with no relief at all for travellers under 17. Crew members have much smaller limits: 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of smoking tobacco.

At Larnaca and Paphos airports and Limassol port, a red and green channel system applies. Use the green channel only if you carry no more than the allowances and no restricted goods; otherwise declare in the red channel. The page was last updated on 5 February 2020, so confirm current figures with headquarters@customs.mof.gov.cy.
cyprus.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Cyprus Customs and Excise Department, general allowances (mof.gov.cy). Last updated 5 February 2020.
faq: Which Cyprus airports use the red and green channel?
Larnaca and Paphos airports and Limassol port use the red and green channel system, according to the Cyprus Customs and Excise Department.
What tobacco allowance do crew members have in Cyprus?
Crew have 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of smoking tobacco, per the Cyprus Customs page last updated 5 February 2020.

p: German Customs (zoll.de) applies the tobacco allowance to importers aged 17 or over: 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco, including heated tobacco and waterpipe tobacco, mixed in proportion. Tobacco sticks for heating count as cigarettes when they can be smoked directly, so the 200 limit applies to them. Tobacco substitute products for people aged 17 or over count as other goods against the value limit.

The allowance can be used only once per trip, which ends when you return home or reach your holiday destination in Germany, and several people's limits cannot be added together. For tobacco bought in another EU country, German Customs gives guide quantities of 800 cigarettes, 400 cigarillos, 200 cigars, 1 kg of fine-cut tobacco and 800 heated-tobacco sticks, valid only if you carry the goods yourself and they come from normal retail in that country. Goods above that are presumed commercial and can be seized and destroyed.

German Customs also warns that buying or holding tobacco that was smuggled into the EU can be a criminal offence (tax receiving, section 374 of the Fiscal Code), even if bought in another member state. Warning signs are a missing tax stamp or health warning and very low prices.
germany.src: Sources read 15 November 2026: zoll.de, Reisefreimengen and Genussmittel pages. Neither page shows a date.
faq: Do heated tobacco sticks count as cigarettes in Germany?
Yes, when they can be smoked directly, German Customs treats tobacco sticks as cigarettes, so the 200 limit applies to them.
Can I use the German tobacco allowance twice in one trip?
No. German Customs says the allowance can be used only once per trip and the limits of several travellers cannot be added together.

slovenia.h: What the Slovenian Financial Administration adds
p: The Slovenian Financial Administration (FURS) grants relief from import duties, VAT and excise duty only for goods imported occasionally for personal or family use or as presents, whose nature and quantity do not suggest commercial purposes. Travellers under 17 are not entitled to relief on tobacco products.

The allowance is 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos (cigars up to 3 g), 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco, or a proportional mix. For relief purposes, an air or sea traveller is anyone travelling for purposes other than private pleasure flying or pleasure sea navigation. The page shows that it was refreshed on 23 September 2020 and says nothing about parcels.
faq: Who counts as a traveller for the Slovenian allowance by air or sea?
The Slovenian Financial Administration says it is anyone travelling by air or sea for purposes other than private pleasure flying or private pleasure sea navigation.
Can Slovenian tobacco relief be used for goods that look commercial?
No. FURS says the nature and quantity of the goods must not indicate that they are imported for commercial purposes.
slovenia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Slovenian Financial Administration, Import of alcoholic beverages and tobacco products (fu.gov.si), refreshed 23 September 2020.

spain.h: What the Spanish Tax Agency adds
p: The Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Tributaria) sets the same tobacco quantities for all arrivals from outside the EU (200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco) but adds local rules. Residents and workers in the Gibraltar border area, meaning Spanish territory within 15 km of the border plus any municipality partly inside that zone, get only 80 cigarettes.

International transport staff on professional journeys have both the quantities and the value thresholds cut to one tenth. The Canary Islands, though in the EU customs territory, apply the same tobacco quantities. Andorra has its own larger limit of 300 cigarettes. The page was last updated on 23 September 2026.
faq: What is the tobacco allowance for the Gibraltar border area in Spain?
Residents and workers in the Gibraltar border area get 80 cigarettes, according to the Spanish Tax Agency. The area is Spanish territory within 15 km of the border.
Do Spain's Canary Islands have a different tobacco allowance?
No. The Spanish Tax Agency lists the same tobacco quantities for the Canary Islands, though IGIC applies instead of VAT.
spain.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Agencia Tributaria, Franchises: tobacco, alcohol and other goods (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es), updated 23 September 2026.

p: Dutch Customs applies the allowance to travellers aged 17 or older, and treats Turkey and the Canary Islands like non-EU origins. Only one carton of 200 cigarettes is allowed, and mixing products reduces each allowance proportionally. From another EU country or Northern Ireland the limits are 800 cigarettes (up to four cartons), 200 cigars, 1 kg of tobacco and 400 cigarillos, and above those you need proof of personal use, such as receipts.

Dutch Customs states that a carton of up to 200 cigarettes incurs over EUR 100 in duties, excise and VAT, and that failing to declare excess goods brings a fine on top. By air or sea use the goods-to-declare exit; by land declare at a customs office at the border. Crew from non-EU countries may bring 40 cigarettes or 50 g of rolling tobacco. E-cigarettes, snus and nicotine pouches may be for personal use only, never for sale. Page updated 9 November 2026.
faq: How many cartons of cigarettes can I bring into the Netherlands from outside the EU?
Only one carton of 200 cigarettes, says Dutch Customs, and mixing products reduces each allowance proportionally.
What does Dutch Customs say about e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches?
They may be brought only for personal use. Selling or distributing e-cigarettes, snus or nicotine pouches is not allowed.
netherlands.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Dutch Customs (douane.nl), cigarettes or tobacco from abroad, updated 9 November 2026.

denmark.h: What the Danish Customs Agency adds
p: The Danish Customs Agency (Toldstyrelsen) says you must be 17 to bring tobacco or alcohol into Denmark, and the tobacco options are alternatives: 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos (max 3 g each), 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco.

Tobacco does not count toward Denmark's value threshold for other goods, which is DKK 3,250 if you arrive by plane or ship and DKK 2,250 by other transport. Above the thresholds, customs duty, VAT and excise duty are due.
faq: What is the minimum age to bring tobacco into Denmark?
The Danish Customs Agency says you must be 17 years old to bring alcohol and tobacco into Denmark.
Does tobacco count toward the Danish value limit?
No. Alcohol and tobacco do not count toward the DKK 3,250 (plane or ship) or DKK 2,250 (other transport) threshold.
denmark.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Danish Customs Agency (toldst.dk), customs rules when travelling to countries outside the EU.

p: Irish Revenue allows 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco from outside the EU, and says tobacco allowances can be split fractionally: 100 cigarettes with 50 cigarillos is fine. Crew on transport have 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g.

Importing oral smokeless tobacco into Ireland is generally prohibited, and Revenue refers readers to its separate prohibitions guidance. Customs duty, excise and VAT are charged on tobacco above the allowances. The page is dated 22 December 2025 and states no age limit for tobacco.
faq: Can I bring snus or oral smokeless tobacco into Ireland?
Irish Revenue says importing oral smokeless tobacco is generally prohibited and points to its prohibitions and restrictions guidance.
Can I split the Irish tobacco allowance between products?
Yes. Revenue's example is 100 cigarettes together with 50 cigarillos.
ireland.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Irish Revenue (revenue.ie), duty-free allowances from outside the EU, dated 22 December 2025.

italy.h: What the Italian Customs and Monopolies Agency adds
p: Italy's Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli, in its traveller customs guide of July 2025, allows 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos (max 3 g each), 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco from outside the EU, each figure counting as 100% so combinations are fine if the percentages add up to no more than 100%. Travellers under 17 are excluded from the exemption.

Tobacco is outside the general value limit of EUR 300, or EUR 430 by air or sea and EUR 150 under 15. If the value of a good exceeds the limit, duty is due on its whole value. While you complete customs formalities you may leave goods above the allowance in customs custody for 90 days, after which uncollected goods are declared abandoned. For travel inside the EU the guide gives indicative thresholds of 800 cigarettes.
faq: Can I leave excess tobacco in custody at Italian customs?
Yes. Italy's customs agency says goods above the allowance can be left in custody for 90 days; unclaimed goods are declared abandoned.
What happens if a good is over the Italian value limit?
Duty is due on the whole value of that good, not only on the excess, according to the Italian customs traveller guide.
italy.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli, Carta doganale del viaggiatore (July 2025 edition).

hungary.h: What the Hungarian tax authority (NAV) adds
p: The Hungarian National Tax and Customs Administration (NAV) lets only travellers aged 17 or over bring tobacco, and its limits differ by transport. Arriving by plane from outside the EU you may bring one of: 200 cigarettes (10 packs), 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars, 250 g of smoking tobacco, 125 g of smokeless tobacco, 125 g of a nicotine product that replaces smoking, 75 ml of e-liquid or 200 heated-tobacco products.

By road, rail or other transport the limits are much lower: 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars, 50 g of smoking tobacco, 25 g of smokeless tobacco, 25 g of a nicotine product, 15 ml of e-liquid or 40 heated-tobacco products. Products are mixed proportionally: 20 cigarettes use half the road limit, leaving room for 5 cigars. A 200-cigarette duty-free carton is within the air limit but exceeds the road limit.

Excess must be declared on entry, with customs duty, VAT and excise tax paid on it. If it is not declared, NAV can impose a customs administrative fine and seize the amount above the allowance. The page shows no update date, only a 2026 copyright.
faq: How much e-liquid can I bring into Hungary?
NAV allows 75 ml of e-liquid when arriving by plane from outside the EU, and 15 ml by road, rail or other transport.
Is a duty-free carton of 200 cigarettes allowed in Hungary by road?
No. NAV says a 200-cigarette carton is within the air limit but exceeds the 40-cigarette limit for road or rail arrivals.
hungary.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Hungarian National Tax and Customs Administration, tobacco products traveller information (nav.gov.hu). The page shows no update date.

p: Swedish Customs (Tullverket) sets the minimum age for tobacco and nicotine products at 18, and says you must have bought them and carry them yourself, for your or your family's own use. For arrivals from outside the EU, a resident of Sweden gets the full allowance only if abroad at least 20 hours or arriving by commercial air: 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars, 250 g of smoking tobacco or 250 g of other tobacco, or a proportional mix. If abroad under 20 hours the limit is 40 cigarettes, 20 cigars or cigarillos or 100 g of other tobacco products, snus included.

E-liquid, snus and other nicotine products are limited by value from outside the EU: goods up to SEK 5,000 for commercial air or ferry travellers and SEK 3,500 for others, covering everything bought on the trip. From another EU country there is no fixed duty-free amount for tobacco, snus is for personal use only and other nicotine products such as pouches, gum or spray are limited to 200 g. Åland and the Canary Islands count as outside the EU fiscal territory. The page was last updated on 25 September 2026.
faq: What is the minimum age for tobacco in Sweden?
Swedish Customs says you must be at least 18 years old for tobacco and nicotine products.
How long must I be abroad to get the full Swedish tobacco allowance?
A resident must have been abroad at least 20 hours or arrive by commercial air transport; under 20 hours the limit is 40 cigarettes or 100 g of other tobacco products.
sweden.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Swedish Customs (tullverket.se), buying tobacco and other nicotine-containing products when travelling, updated 25 September 2026.

estonia.h: What the Estonian Tax and Customs Board adds
p: The Estonian Tax and Customs Board (EMTA) sets the minimum age for the tobacco and alcohol exemptions at 18, not 17, and ties the allowance to how often you cross the border. On the first and second entry in a calendar month you may bring 40 cigarettes (200 by air), 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars, 50 g of smoking tobacco including up to 20 g of heated tobacco (250 g and 100 g by air), 120 g of solid tobacco substitute including tobacco-free snus, 20 ml of tobacco liquid, 20 g of another alternative tobacco product or one smokeless tobacco package of up to 50 g.

On a third entry in a month, EMTA may grant an extra exemption (not for smokeless tobacco) if you can show the import was occasional. Air, train and sea travellers are not limited by border-crossing frequency. Cigarettes, cigarillos and cigars may only be brought in if they are not produced in Russia and not brought from Russia, because EU sanctions prohibit tobacco imports from Russia. The page was last updated on 27 October 2026.
faq: What is the minimum age for tobacco allowances in Estonia?
Estonia's Tax and Customs Board says travellers must be at least 18 years old to bring in tobacco and alcohol under these exemptions.
Can I bring tobacco into Estonia from Russia?
Only if it was not produced in Russia and not brought from Russia; EU sanctions prohibit importing tobacco products from Russia.
estonia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Estonian Tax and Customs Board (emta.ee), From a third country to Estonia, updated 27 October 2026.

latvia.h: What Latvia's State Revenue Service adds
p: Latvia's State Revenue Service (VID) lets travellers bring tobacco from a third country duty-free no more than once every 30 days. By road, rail or sea the limit is 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of smoking tobacco, tobacco leaves or heated tobacco; by air it is 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g. Products can be mixed if the percentages total no more than 100%.

Persons under 20 may not bring in tobacco products, tobacco substitutes, herbal smoking products, electronic smoking devices or refill containers. The page gives no quantity allowance for e-cigarettes. EU sanctions bar cigarettes, cigarillos and cigars from Russia and Belarus. Goods above the limit must be declared in the red channel, and undeclared goods can bring a warning or a fine of up to EUR 2,000, and possibly criminal liability. Page updated 22 April 2025.
faq: How often can I bring duty-free tobacco into Latvia?
Latvia's State Revenue Service says not more frequently than once every 30 days.
What is the minimum age for tobacco and e-cigarettes in Latvia?
Persons under 20 may not bring in tobacco products, tobacco substitute products, herbal smoking products, electronic smoking devices or refill containers, says VID.
latvia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Latvian State Revenue Service (vid.gov.lv), Excise goods, updated 22 April 2025.

p: Luxembourg Customs (douanes.public.lu) gives 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of loose tobacco for travellers arriving directly from outside the EU, mixed proportionally within the tobacco category; for example half the cigarette allowance can be swapped for 50 cigarillos, or for 25 cigarillos and 12 cigars.

E-liquids, heated tobacco and nicotine pouches are not in the tobacco allowance: they fall under 'other goods' with perfume, coffee and tea, and so count against the value limit of EUR 430 by air or sea and EUR 300 for other travellers. Travellers under 17 cannot bring tobacco or alcohol duty-free, and under-15s have EUR 175 for other goods. Allowances cannot be pooled between people for a single item, and an item above the limit must be declared and taxed on its full value. Page updated 30 July 2026.
faq: Do e-liquids and nicotine pouches count in the Luxembourg tobacco allowance?
No. Luxembourg Customs puts e-liquids, heated tobacco and nicotine pouches under 'other goods', subject to the EUR 430 or EUR 300 value limit.
Can a family pool its allowance for one expensive item in Luxembourg?
No. The page says allowances cannot be pooled between people for one item; a family of four cannot claim a EUR 1,720 item duty-free.
luxembourg.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Luxembourg Customs (douanes.public.lu), arriving from a country outside the EU, updated 30 July 2026.

p: French Customs says the non-EU tobacco quantities (200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco) cannot be cumulated, but a proportional assortment is allowed: using half the cigarette allowance leaves half of the cigarillo, cigar or smoking tobacco allowance. Travellers under 17 are excluded, and so are cross-border and international transport workers under 18.

Those workers have lower quantities: 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of smoking tobacco. For arrivals from overseas departments, the Channel Islands or the Canary Islands customs duties are not due, but VAT applies above the value thresholds and VAT and excise are due above the quantity allowances. French Customs adds that tobacco bought on a website is prohibited and will be confiscated before delivery. Page updated 6 August 2026.
faq: Can I buy tobacco from a website and have it delivered to France?
No. French Customs says tobacco bought on a website is prohibited and will be confiscated before delivery.
Can I add up the French tobacco allowances for cigarettes and cigars?
No, the quantities cannot be cumulated, but a proportional assortment is allowed, for example half the cigarette allowance plus half the cigar allowance.
france.src: Source read 15 November 2026: French Customs (douane.gouv.fr), customs and tax exemptions in quantities and values, updated 6 August 2026.

brazil.h: What the Brazilian Federal Revenue says about tobacco in baggage
p: The Brazilian Federal Revenue (Receita Federal) traveller guide sets tobacco limits inside the baggage exemption: 10 packs of 20 foreign-made cigarettes, 25 cigars or cigarillos in total, and 250 grams of loose tobacco, by air, sea or land. The arrival Free Shop has its own limits, 20 packs of cigarettes, 25 cigars or cigarillos and 250 grams of tobacco prepared for pipes. People under 18 cannot buy tobacco products at Free Shops, even when accompanied.

The money quota is separate: US$1,000 for air or sea arrivals and US$500 for other routes, per person, not transferable and granted every 30 days, plus an extra US$1,000 at the first Brazilian airport's arrival Free Shop and US$500 every 30 days at land Free Shops. Purchases above the extra quota are taxed under the special RTE regime, and goods above the quantity limits are treated as ordinary baggage and lose the tax exemption. Exempt goods generally need not be declared because they do not count toward the quota. Goods bought at departure Free Shops do count toward the quota.
brazil.src: Source read: Receita Federal, Cota de isenção, duty free e bagagem tributável (in Portuguese).

canada.h: What the Canada Border Services Agency says about tobacco
p: The Canada Border Services Agency says non-residents and temporary residents must declare all tobacco and vaping products when they enter Canada, and the minimum age is 18 wherever you enter. The quantity limits are 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars, 200 grams of manufactured tobacco or 200 tobacco sticks, and 12 vaping containers or fewer with a maximum of 120 mL of liquid or 120 g of solid.

The page does not call tobacco within these limits duty-free. It says duties and taxes could apply to limited quantities and that you should be ready to pay them on any declared amount, so the allowance is a limit on quantity, not a promise of no tax. Amounts above the limits may need a permit from the provincial or territorial authority. Tobacco, vaping products and alcohol cannot count as exempt gifts of under CAD 60. The page does not state a penalty for undeclared tobacco, since the penalty of up to CAD 1,300 it mentions applies to undeclared food, plants and animals.
canada.src: Source read: CBSA, What can I bring: tobacco and vaping products for non-residents. No penalty for undeclared tobacco is stated.

cambodia.h: What the Cambodia Airports customs page says about tobacco
p: The customs and excise page of Cambodia Airports says an arriving passenger may bring one of the following: up to 200 cigarettes, up to 50 cigars or up to 250 grams of tobacco. It says passengers under 18 are not allowed to carry tobacco or alcohol. Our card also notes that the Ministry of Tourism's site gives a higher figure, so plan on the lower one.

The same page lists up to 2 litres of alcohol and 350 ml of perfume and cosmetics. Goods worth US$100 or more are subject to duties and taxes, and a false declaration or using the green channel to avoid declaring dutiable goods can lead to fines or prosecution. The page is an airport operator's summary, not the Cambodian customs department, and tells you to check the official customs regulations, which is why the card is marked unofficial.
cambodia.src: Source read: Cambodia Airports, Customs and excise. This is an airport operator page and is an unofficial source.

argentina.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in Argentina
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Argentina allows 400 cigarettes and 50 cigars, or 200 cigarettes and 25 cigars when coming from Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay or Uruguay. Travellers under 18 get half of these amounts.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
argentina.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Argentina (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

australia.h: What Sydney Airport says about tobacco
p: Sydney Airport’s information sheet says adults (18 or over) can bring one unopened packet of up to 25 cigarettes, or 25 g of tobacco products, plus one opened packet. It also mentions up to 1.5 kg of smokeless tobacco for personal use. Duty applies to tobacco above 25 g.
The sheet shows no update date and comes from an airport operator, not from the Australian Border Force, so confirm on the Border Force website before you fly.
australia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Sydney Airport, duty-free allowances for arriving passengers (airport operator page, undated). The Australian Border Force page could not be opened.

bahrain.h: What Bahrain Customs says about tobacco, e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches
p: Bahrain Customs Affairs, on its page "Duty Free Allowances" (read from an archived copy on 24 November 2026), exempts personal effects and gifts carried by travellers if they are not commercial and worth no more than BD 300. For tobacco it lists 400 regular or electronically heated cigarettes, or the equivalent of 250 g of tobacco, or 400 nicotine pouches; 50 cigars; and a quarter of a kilo of pipe tobacco.

The same list allows ten electronic cigarettes, one electronic heating device, one electronic hookah device and 60 ml of liquid for electronic hookah filling, plus 3 litres of alcoholic beverages and 12 cans of beer. Tobacco and alcohol must be in the possession of someone aged 18 or over. The goods must not be commercial, the traveller must not be a frequent flyer bringing goods in regularly, and aircrew follow a separate mechanism. Customs may keep dutiable goods for up to three months at the traveller's request.
bahrain.src: Source read: Bahrain Customs Affairs, Duty Free Allowances (customs.gov.bh), read from an archived copy on 24 November 2026.

belgium.h: What Brussels Airport says about tobacco
p: Brussels Airport's customs page gives travellers from outside the EU up to 200 cigarettes or 250 g of tobacco for the green exit. Above that, use the red exit; if customs finds more than the exempt quantity you pay duties and taxes and a fine.

The page says Belgian customs mainly checks quantities of alcohol, tobacco and perfume and the total value of purchases, and that different limits apply from another EU country. Confirm with Belgian customs.
belgium.src: Reliable unofficial source, read 22 November 2026: Brussels Airport customs page. It is the airport operator's page, not Belgian customs, which it points to for full details.

bulgaria.h: What the Bulgarian Customs Agency says about tobacco
p: The Bulgarian Customs Agency gives the tobacco allowance for travellers over 17 years of age arriving from a third country: 200 cigarettes for air travellers and 40 for all other travellers, 100 or 20 cigarillos, 50 or 10 cigars, and 250 g or 50 g of smoking tobacco. It can be split across products as long as the percentages used add up to no more than 100%. This settles the age question: the agency says over 17, not 18.
Crew of the vehicle you arrive on have only the lower figures: 40 cigarettes, 10 cigars, 20 cigarillos or 50 g of smoking tobacco, whatever the transport.
bulgaria.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Bulgarian Customs Agency, "Brief summary of the monetary thresholds and quantitative limits for goods contained in the personal luggage of travellers coming from third countries and territories" (customs.bg, English page; read from an archived copy because the live site refused our reader).
link: Bulgarian Customs Agency: allowances for travellers from third countries

chile.h: What Chilean Customs says about the tobacco allowance
p: The Chilean customs service says the duty- and tax-free baggage allowance for each adult traveller is 400 cigarettes, 500 grams of pipe tobacco, 50 cigars and 2,500 cubic centimetres of alcoholic drinks. The page does not define the adult age for this baggage rule, but for Duty Free purchases buyers of cigarettes and alcohol must be over 18.

Duty Free shop goods are exempt from duties and internal taxes up to US$675 if non-commercial, must be in sealed packaging, and may not be opened before clearing customs. Gifts up to US$300 apply to travellers over 14. Personal imports without a customs agent are allowed up to US$1,500, with 6% duty and 19% VAT. Cash above US$10,000 must be declared. We read the first 100,000 characters of a long page, and the penalties for tobacco are not in the part read.
chile.src: Source read: Aduanas de Chile, Preguntas frecuentes viajero y turista (in Spanish), first 100,000 characters.

dominican-republic.h: What the Dominican customs traveller manual says about tobacco
p: The Dominican customs traveller manual lists as duty-free tobacco 20 packs of cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 200 grams of tobacco, and you may choose one of the three. It sets the adult threshold only for alcohol, up to 5 litres of drinks, and gives no numeric age for tobacco, so ask Customs about minors.

Gifts up to US$500 are allowed, once every three months, and anything above must be declared. Each traveller may bring one laptop and one tablet duty-free, and children up to 5 toys. Items above the allowances are subject to taxes. The manual also tells travellers to declare cash over US$10,000. It does not list a penalty for exceeding the tobacco allowance.
dominican-republic.src: Source read: DGA, Manual del Viajero (in Spanish). No tobacco penalty is stated.

fiji.h: What Fiji Revenue and Customs says about tobacco and alcohol
p: The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service says travellers aged 18 or over may bring up to 200 cigarettes, or 200 g of cigars or other tobacco, or a mix totalling no more than 200 g, duty-free, and e-cigarette liquid is capped at 200 ml or mg. Chewing tobacco is prohibited. The items must be carried by the traveller and not be for sale or for someone else. The alcohol allowance is up to 3 litres of spirits, 4.5 litres of wine or 4.5 litres of beer, or a mix within the same total.

Personal goods valued at FJ$2,000 or less are duty-free if for your own use, and Gold Card holders have the same tobacco and alcohol limits with a FJ$3,000 value cap on other goods. Goods over the allowance, or for commercial use, are subject to duty. On the arrival card you tick Yes in the Customs section for prohibited or restricted items, FJ$10,000 or more in currency or biosecurity risk goods, and the page does not list tobacco as a separate trigger.
fiji.src: Source read: FRCS, Arriving in Fiji. It gives no penalty for tobacco over the allowance.

egypt.h: What the Egyptian Customs Authority says about tourists and tobacco
p: The Egyptian Customs Authority page for tourists and transit passengers says a tourist may bring one carton of cigarettes, which is 200 cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 200 g of tobacco, plus one litre of spirits, and duties and taxes apply to anything above. Residents have the same allowance. The page does not say that the tobacco is recorded in the passport, which our card mentions, so ask Customs about that.

Tourists may also buy goods in customs-zone shops within 48 hours of arrival, up to US$200 in total, up to 3 litres of spirits with the first two litres at 1% of the customs duty and the third at 25%, and up to 2 cartons of cigarettes. That allowance can be claimed up to four times a year with the passport holder present, and each family member has their own. New goods up to EGP 15,000 are exempt if not for trade.
egypt.src: Source read: Egyptian Customs Authority, Travel and tourism (in Arabic). The passport record is not mentioned on the page.

georgia.h: What the Georgian Revenue Service brochure says about tobacco
p: The Georgian Revenue Service customs brochure allows, per person, 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 50 cigarillos, or 200 heated tobacco products, or 10 tobacco capsules, or 250 g of other tobacco products except raw tobacco, or a combination if the shares of each product, measured against its own limit, do not add up to more than 100%, or 50 ml of e-cigarette liquid. By road the allowance is per 30 calendar days, and through air checkpoints it applies per calendar day, for personal or family use or as a gift.

Tax benefits for tobacco and alcohol start at age 18. The brochure also lists alcohol limits of 1 litre of spirits of 22% or higher, and 16 litres of beer. Goods up to GEL 500 and 30 kg may be imported duty-free per 30 days by road, and up to GEL 3,000 through air checkpoints. It does not describe penalties for tobacco.
georgia.src: Source read: Revenue Service of Georgia, brochure on exemption of goods from duties and declaring. It states no tobacco penalty.

ethiopia.h: What the Ethiopian Ministry of Finance directive says about tobacco
p: Ethiopian Ministry of Finance Directive No. 923/2014 on goods imported or exported for personal use, circulated in 2022, says any traveller may import for personal use, without duty or tax, 200 grams of cigarettes, which it also gives as 20 pieces, and 250 grams of loose tobacco, plus 2 litres of alcohol. The table sits next to perfume allowances.

The directive is about travellers' goods in general and the file we read is held on an airline's site, not the customs commission's, which is why the card is marked unofficial. It does not list a penalty for tobacco, and a limit of 20 cigarettes is far below the EU figure, so check the current rules with the Ethiopian Customs Commission.
ethiopia.src: Source read: Ethiopian Ministry of Finance Directive No. 923/2014 (English copy on ethiopianairlines.com). It is an unofficial copy and states no tobacco penalty.

cuba.h: What the Cuban tourism portal says about tobacco in personal effects
p: The Cuban tourism portal lists, per adult, up to 400 cigarettes, 500 g of pipe tobacco and 50 Cuban cigars, and 2,500 cc of alcoholic drinks among the personal effects a traveller may bring. It says quantities above those listed for each item are not treated as personal effects and are subject to the rules for imported goods. Under the weight and value method, 25 kg of goods count as personal effects and pay no customs duty.

The page also lists medicines for personal use with a prescription, and extra items for foreign tourists such as a portable computer and camping gear. It is a tourism portal, not Cuban Customs, which is why the card is marked unofficial, and it does not give an age limit or a penalty. Check Cuban Customs, whose own site would not open securely for us earlier, before you travel.
cuba.src: Source read: cuba.travel, Accessories for traveling. This is a tourism portal and an unofficial source.

china.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in China
p: The Travel Doc customs page for China allows travellers aged 16 and over 400 cigarettes, 100 cigars and 500 g of tobacco.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
china.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for China (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

colombia.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in Colombia
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Colombia allows travellers aged 18 and over one of: 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars or 250 g of tobacco.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
colombia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Colombia (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

costa-rica.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in Costa Rica
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Costa Rica lists 500 grams of tobacco products as free to import.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
costa-rica.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Costa Rica (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.
link: Travel Doc: Costa Rica customs information

hong-kong.h: What Hong Kong Customs says about the tobacco concession
p: Hong Kong Customs and Excise says travellers aged 18 or over may bring 19 cigarettes, or 1 cigar, or 25 g of cigars, or 25 g of other manufactured tobacco duty-free, which is one of the smallest allowances in the world. The liquor concession is 1 litre of liquor above 30% alcohol by volume, and a Hong Kong ID card holder must have been outside Hong Kong for at least 24 hours to use it. Hong Kong charges excise duty only on liquor, tobacco, hydrocarbon oil and methyl alcohol.

Failing to declare dutiable goods above the allowance, or making a false or incomplete declaration, can lead to prosecution, or the department may instead impose a penalty for compoundable offences under Cap. 109. There is no concession for goods for trade or business, and anyone carrying such goods must use the Red Channel, declare the purpose and lodge import declarations. Cross-boundary drivers under the Northbound and Southbound schemes are not eligible.
hong-kong.src: Source read: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department, Duty-free concessions for passengers. The penalty amounts are not on the page.

iceland.h: What Icelandic Customs says about the tobacco allowance and ages
p: Icelandic Customs (Skatturinn) allows 200 cigarettes, or 250 g of other tobacco products, duty-free. The minimum age for bringing tobacco is 18, while the minimum age for alcohol is 20. Alcohol combinations the page gives include 1 litre of spirits, 0.75 litre of wine and 3 litres of beer, or 18 litres of beer, with spirits meaning drinks above 21% alcohol.

The goods must be for personal use or as gifts, not for sale, and travel agencies, guides or drivers cannot import duty-free goods on a traveller's behalf. Food is limited to 10 kg and ISK 25,000, and Icelandic residents may bring goods worth up to ISK 88,000 in total, with children under 12 getting half. Use the red channel if you have dutiable or restricted goods or are unsure. The page does not state a penalty for tobacco over the allowance.
iceland.src: Source read: Skatturinn, Duty-free imports (English). No penalty for tobacco is stated.

india.h: What the Indian customs passenger guide says about cigarettes and tobacco
p: The Indian customs passenger guide allows, within the duty-free allowance for incoming passengers, 100 cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 125 g of tobacco, next to 2 litres of alcohol, on the condition that the goods carry the pictorial health warning prescribed under the cigarettes and tobacco packaging and labelling rules of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

Above the allowance the guide gives the rate for cigarettes as basic customs duty of 60% plus a social welfare surcharge of 10% and the other applicable duties and taxes, and for alcohol other than beer 50% plus an agriculture infrastructure cess. These rates come from a guide that may be out of date, so check the current rates with Indian customs before you carry more than the allowance.
india.src: Source read: CBIC, Customs clearance of passengers at a glance (PDF). The rates may have changed since the guide was issued.

jamaica.h: What the Jamaica Customs Agency says about tobacco
p: The Jamaica Customs Agency page on duty-free allowances says travellers aged 18 and over may bring 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 230 grams of processed tobacco, with 2 litres of alcohol, 170 ml of perfume and 340 ml of eau de toilette. Items must be properly declared, and each allowance applies only up to the stated amount.

Personal and household effects, including gifts, are exempt up to US$1,000 or the equivalent in Jamaican dollars. The page does not describe penalties for going over the tobacco allowance or the age rule for travellers under 18, so ask Customs before you travel with more.
jamaica.src: Source read: Jamaica Customs Agency, What are my duty-free allowances and exemptions. No tobacco penalty is stated.

japan.h: What Japan Customs says about the tobacco allowance and age
p: Japan Customs lists the duty-free allowance per person over 20 as 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 10 packages of heat-not-burn tobacco, or 250 g of other tobacco products. The page applies the allowances only to people over 20 and says nothing about younger travellers. Alcohol is 3 bottles of 760 ml, and other items are allowed in any quantity as long as each item's overseas market value is 10,000 yen or less, up to 200,000 yen in total.

An item worth more than 200,000 yen gets no allowance and is taxed in full, and customs applies the allowance to the items that benefit the traveller most. The page does not state the duty rates or the procedure for quantities above the allowance.
japan.src: Source read: Japan Customs, Customs Answer 7104 (English). Duty rates above the allowance are not on the page.

kenya.h: What the Kenya Revenue Authority says about tobacco
p: The Kenya Revenue Authority says cigarettes, cigars, cheroots, cigarillos, tobacco and snuff are allowed up to 250 grams combined without exemption, and duty-free shop purchases on planes or ships must be declared if they exceed that. The alcohol limits are 1 litre of spirits and 2 litres of wine, and perfume up to half a litre.

Passengers get a US$2,000 concession for personal or household goods, but alcohol, perfume and tobacco are not covered by it beyond those limits. Goods bought abroad above US$500 must be declared, and the Red Channel is for dutiable or restricted goods. Failing to declare or misdeclaring goods breaches Section 203 of the East African Community Customs Management Act and goods are liable to seizure or confiscation.
kenya.src: Source read: KRA, Passenger terminal clearance in Kenya.

israel.h: What the Israel Tax Authority says about tobacco
p: The Israel Tax Authority says that entering Israel through an airport or land border after a stay of at least 3 days abroad you may bring 250 grams of tobacco (one pack) tax-free, on top of 1 litre of alcohol, 2 litres of wine, 250 ml of perfume and goods worth up to 200 US dollars. The page gives no cigarette count.

The Travel Doc customs page (unofficial) says 250 g of any tobacco product up to a maximum of 200 cigarettes, for travellers aged 18 and over. Confirm the age and the cigarette count with customs before you travel.
israel.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Israel Tax Authority, "Information for Israeli residents wishing to import goods in personal import" (gov.il, English, published 22 October 2025). The Travel Doc page (unofficial, read 16 November 2026) gives the age.
link: Israel Tax Authority: personal import, entering by airport or land border

indonesia.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in Indonesia
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Indonesia lists a duty-free allowance of 200 cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 100 g of tobacco. It states no age limit.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
indonesia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Indonesia (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

kuwait.h: Tobacco in Kuwait: the card, an unofficial source and the general rule
p: Our card says personal effects and gifts worth up to 3,000 Saudi riyals, or the same value in another GCC currency, are exempt, and that the exemption includes up to 400 cigarettes. It comes from the GCC customs law as published on the Kuwait customs site that we link below the card.

The official page could not be re-opened, and the UK government's travel advice for Kuwait, which we also read, says nothing about tobacco. So this section applies the general rule most countries follow: duty-free tobacco allowances are commonly about 200 cigarettes, or a matching weight of other tobacco, for adults, and anything above is taxed or confiscated. For Kuwait we have only the card figure, so confirm it with Kuwait Customs.
kuwait.src: Official page not re-opened; the UK government (FCDO) advice read on 16 November 2026 does not cover tobacco. Global rule applied, unofficial.

mexico.h: What the Mexican customs agency says about the tobacco allowance
p: The Mexican customs agency (ANAM) says passengers over 18 may bring up to 20 packs of cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 200 g of tobacco duty-free in their personal luggage, plus up to 3 litres of alcoholic drinks and 6 litres of wine. Separately, passengers may bring goods worth up to US$500 beyond personal luggage if an invoice or receipt supports the value, and family members arriving together on the same transport can combine the exemption.

That US$500 exemption does not cover alcoholic drinks, manufactured tobacco or fuel beyond the vehicle's tank. Customs staff may set the value if there is no receipt, and goods bought in the border strip still count toward the limit if you show the tax receipt. The page also names the Heroes Paisanos periods for Mexicans returning for holidays and lists up to three pets with a zoosanitary certificate. It does not describe penalties for exceeding the tobacco allowance.
mexico.src: Source read: ANAM, Equipaje y franquicia (English). No tobacco penalty is stated.

new-zealand.h: What New Zealand Customs says about tobacco and duty
p: New Zealand Customs says you can bring in 50 cigarettes, or 50 g of cigars or tobacco products, or 50 g of a mix, and must be 17 or older to claim alcohol and tobacco concessions, while you must be 18 to buy them in New Zealand. Anything above must be declared, and duty and GST are payable on the excess. Undeclared excess is seized and destroyed, and you may be fined or prosecuted. If you do not want to pay, unwanted tobacco can be left in the airport disposal bins, where it is destroyed.

The NZ$700 goods concession is separate, with alcohol and tobacco having their own limits, and travelling companions cannot pool their concessions. The alcohol concession is 4.5 litres of wine or beer, or 3 bottles of spirits or liqueur of no more than 1.125 litres each, for personal use and gifts only. The tobacco limit applies when you leave a cruise ship. Anything over your concession is charged full duties, and the Customs estimator tool shows likely charges.
new-zealand.src: Source read: New Zealand Customs, Duty-free shopping.

norway.h: What Norwegian Customs says about tobacco quotas
p: Norwegian Customs gives visitors who live outside Norway a quota of 200 cigarettes or 250 g of other tobacco, plus 200 cigarette papers, while residents of Norway get 100 cigarettes or 125 g, plus 100 papers. Snuff, cigars and cigarillos are counted by weight, and duty-free shops at Norwegian airports sell only the resident amount. You must be 18 or older to bring beer, wine and tobacco and 20 or older to bring drinks above 22% alcohol.

Quotas are per person and can be combined with alcohol, but tobacco cannot be exchanged for alcohol. The alcohol quotas are 1 litre of spirits, 1.5 litres of wine and 2 litres of beer, and one litre of spirits can be swapped for 1.5 litres of wine or beer. You may bring more than the quota but must declare the excess on a simplified customs declaration. Unapproved new tobacco and nicotine products, such as nicotine pouches and heated tobacco, waterpipe tobacco and some e-cigarettes are not allowed. The page does not describe penalties.
norway.src: Source read: Toll.no, Alcohol and tobacco quotas (English). No penalty is stated on the page.

maldives.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in the Maldives
p: The Travel Doc customs page for the Maldives lists a duty-free allowance of 200 cigarettes, 25 cigars and 250 g of tobacco. It adds that all tobacco products must carry a health warning label prescribed by the Ministry of Health.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
maldives.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for the Maldives (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.
link: Travel Doc: the Maldives customs information

mauritius.h: What the Mauritius Revenue Authority says about tobacco and alcohol
p: The Mauritius Revenue Authority (MRA) page "Allowances", with rules in force from 1 September 2025, says a passenger aged 18 or over may bring 250 grams of tobacco, cigarettes and cigars included, and must choose only one of three combinations with it: option A adds 1 litre of spirits and 2 litres of wine, ale or beer; option B adds 2 litres of spirits; option C adds 4 litres of wine, ale or beer.

Duty, excise duty and VAT are payable on any quantity above the allowance. Passengers arriving from Rodrigues have their own values and buy their duty-free goods in a shop at the airport or port on the island of departure. The page limits other accompanied goods by value, Rs 15,000 for foreign passengers on international flights, and these must pass through customs arrival processes.
mauritius.src: Source read: Mauritius Revenue Authority, Allowances (mra.mu), read from an archived copy on 24 November 2026.

nigeria.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in Nigeria
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Nigeria lists 200 grams of all tobacco products as free to import. It states no age limit.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
nigeria.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Nigeria (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

malaysia.h: Tobacco in Malaysia: the card, an unofficial source and the general rule
p: Our card says no duty-free amount is listed and that the Customs Declaration form asks every arriving traveller whether they carry tobacco products, including cigarettes, so you declare any you bring. It comes from a Malaysian customs form that we link below the card.

The official page could not be re-opened, and the UK government's travel advice for Malaysia, which we also read, says nothing about tobacco. So this section applies the general rule most countries follow: the usual global rule is a single small tobacco allowance per adult traveller. For Malaysia, plan on the card figure and check the Royal Malaysian Customs Department for age limits and what happens above it.
malaysia.src: Official page not re-opened; the UK government (FCDO) advice read on 16 November 2026 does not cover tobacco. Global rule applied, unofficial.

morocco.h: What the Moroccan Customs and Indirect Taxes Administration says about tobacco
p: The Administration des Douanes et Impôts Indirects (ADII) traveller guide for people arriving in Morocco (douane.gov.ma, read from an archived copy on 24 November 2026) says visitors may import, free of duties and taxes and without declaration or customs formalities, 200 grams of manufactured tobacco. It counts weight, not a number of cigarettes, and gives no age limit.

On the same list the guide allows one bottle of perfume (150 ml) and one of eau de toilette (250 ml), one 1-litre bottle of wine and one 1-litre bottle of spirits, and non-commercial objects up to a total value of 2,000 dirhams. Anything beyond these tolerances is subject to duties and taxes, and a receipt is given when you pay. The guide adds that personal medicines are admitted duty-free without prior ministry permission, with a signed undertaking and a prescription or medical certificate, and that plant products need a phytosanitary certificate. It does not mention e-cigarettes.
morocco.src: Source read: ADII, guide for travellers arriving in Morocco (douane.gov.ma, PDF), read from an archived copy on 24 November 2026. The guide is undated.
link: ADII (Moroccan customs): guide for travellers arriving in Morocco

nepal.h: What the Nepal aeronautical information publication says about tobacco
p: The passenger customs section of the Nepal aeronautical information publication says no customs duty is levied on goods brought by a foreign passenger holding a passport up to: one bottle of liquor of up to one litre or up to twelve cans of beer, up to 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars and 250 grams of tobacco, medicines up to NPR 10,000, foodstuffs up to NPR 5,000 and fresh fruit up to NPR 2,000.

The publication is an aviation document of the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal, not a page of the Customs Department, so it does not give an age limit or a penalty for going over the allowance. The wording says up to 200 sticks, 50 sticks of cigars and 250 grams, and it does not say whether the three can be combined, so ask Nepal Customs before you carry a mix.
nepal.src: Source read: Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal, AIP Nepal, customs section. It gives no age limit or penalty.

sri-lanka.h: What Sri Lanka Customs says about tobacco and the baggage allowances
p: Sri Lanka Customs says cigarettes, cigars, beedies and snuff are not allowed as personal baggage, whether accompanied or unaccompanied, and the page describes no permit route for tobacco. Foreigners may bring 1.5 litres of liquor, and residents 2.5 litres, which must be bought at Sri Lanka Duty Free shops or carried from abroad on the day of arrival.

The general allowances apply to Sri Lankan passport holders, residence visa holders and qualifying dual citizens, based on time abroad: for adults, US$125, US$500 or US$1,000 depending on whether the stay was under 90 days, 90 to 365 days or over 365 days, with higher figures including duty-free shop purchases. Airline crew get none. The page also covers permits for plants and animals, a US$200 fee per person for declared gemstones, and currency declarations above US$15,000 on entry and US$10,000 on exit.
sri-lanka.src: Source read: Sri Lanka Customs, Passenger Services Directorate. It gives no penalty for tobacco.

singapore.h: What Singapore Customs says about tobacco and the alcohol concession
p: Singapore Customs says no duty-free concession or GST relief applies to tobacco: cigarettes and tobacco products are subject to duty and GST, including packs bought in Singapore with the SDPC mark. Since 1 July 2020, imports must meet standardised packaging requirements, and non-compliant products are disposed of at checkpoints. The page does not state the duty per stick and refers to a separate duty rates page.

Failing to declare goods at the Red Channel may result in fines or prosecution, and you must declare goods above your concessions, including those carried for others. The alcohol concession needs you to be 18 or older, to have been abroad at least 2 days and not be arriving from Malaysia, with options such as 1 litre of spirits plus 1 litre of wine, or 2 litres of beer, and more than 10 litres needs a permit. The S$500 GST relief for newly bought goods excludes liquor and tobacco.
singapore.src: Source read: Singapore Customs, Duty-free concession and GST relief. The duty per stick is on another page.

turkey.h: What the Turkish customs guide says about the tobacco allowance
p: The Turkish customs guide says a traveller may bring up to 600 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars, 250 g of cut tobacco with 200 cigarette papers and 250 g of pipe tobacco. Each product has its own quantity limit, and the allowance cannot be exceeded for any single product. Travellers under 18 cannot claim the tobacco or alcohol allowances, and the items must be with the traveller. The alcohol allowance is 1 litre of spirits above 22% or 2 litres of drinks at or below 22%.

The page states no monetary value limit for these allowances, and a related question on its index mentions 1,500 euros for a single item without explaining it. It does not give a penalty for going over, so check Turkish Customs for the current rules, which have changed several times.
turkey.src: Source read: Gümrük Rehberi (Turkish customs guide), traveller allowances (in Turkish). No penalty is stated.

united-kingdom.h: What GOV.UK says about the tobacco allowance for Great Britain
p: GOV.UK says you can bring one of 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars, 250 g of tobacco or 200 sticks for electronic heated tobacco devices into Great Britain, and you can split the allowance across types, for example 100 cigarettes and 25 cigars. If you go over, you pay tax and duty on all of that category, not just the excess. Your goods could be seized if you do not declare them, and you declare online before travelling or at the border.

For travellers aged 17 or under there are no personal allowances for alcohol, tobacco or vaping products; you can bring them for your own use but must declare them before arriving. Other goods are allowed up to GBP 390, or GBP 270 by private plane or boat, and above that you pay tax and duty on the whole value. The alcohol allowance is 42 litres of beer and cider, 18 litres of wine and 4 litres of spirits. The page covers Great Britain only, and Northern Ireland has its own guide.
united-kingdom.src: Source read: GOV.UK, Duty-free goods: arriving in Great Britain.

united-states.h: What U.S. Customs and Border Protection says about tobacco
p: U.S. Customs and Border Protection says returning residents may bring tobacco within their personal exemption, which covers not more than 200 cigarettes and 100 cigars, and the tobacco exemption applies to adults 21 and older. Amounts beyond that can be detained, seized or penalised. One litre of alcohol can count toward the exemption if it is for your own use, not for resale, legal in the state where you arrive, and the traveller is at least 21; states may set stricter limits.

The standard exemption is US$800, and items above it but within the flat-rate limit are dutiable at a flat 3%. The page does not mention a US$100 gift allowance. On Cuba, it says goods from licensed private Cuban entrepreneurs may be imported if they are not on the State Department's prohibited list, with proof of purchase kept and CBP deciding case by case, and personal-use goods under US$800 entering duty-free. It does not specifically address Cuban cigars.
united-states.src: Source read: CBP, Customs duty information for international visitors.

thailand.h: What Thai Customs says about the green channel allowance
p: The Suvarnabhumi Airport customs page for the Nothing to Declare channel allows up to 200 cigarettes, or 250 g of tobacco, or 250 g of all types combined, plus up to 1 litre of alcohol, and personal belongings worth up to 20,000 baht, excluding prohibited or restricted goods and food. Any excess cigarettes, tobacco or alcohol must be put in the box provided by Customs, and the page warns that otherwise prosecution will be carried out.

In the Red Channel you bring your passport and any invoices or receipts, and non-commercial accompanying belongings up to 200,000 baht are assessed a flat rate of duty and taxes. Prohibited or restricted goods lead to prosecution. The page does not mention e-cigarettes, which are the subject of a separate Thai ban, so check the rules on them with Thai Customs before you travel.
thailand.src: Source read: Thai Customs Department, Suvarnabhumi Airport green channel page. E-cigarettes are not covered on it.

taiwan.h: What Taipei Customs says about tobacco and alcohol
p: Taipei Customs says passengers aged 20 or over may bring in duty-free 200 cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 1 pound of smoking tobacco, or 200 government-approved designated tobacco products. The overall limit for tobacco is 1,000 cigarettes, or 125 cigars or 5 pounds of smoking tobacco, with the duty-free amount counted toward it. Passengers aged 18 or over may bring 1.5 litres of alcohol duty-free, with an overall limit of 5 litres, and alcohol declared as of Chinese origin is limited to 1 litre in total.

E-cigarettes and e-liquids are prohibited, as are undeclared or unapproved designated tobacco products, and carrying prohibited goods may lead to criminal penalties. For tobacco and alcohol above the allowance the page gives fines and confiscation, for example NTD 1,000 per 200 cigarettes, and dutiable goods may be confiscated or fined up to three times their value. Used personal articles are limited to NTD 10,000 per piece or set, and tobacco and alcohol are excluded from the NTD 35,000 personal goods limit.
taiwan.src: Source read: Customs Administration, Taipei Customs, duty-free page (English). Rates may have changed, so check the current amounts.

switzerland.h: What the Swiss customs office says about duty-free allowances
p: The Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Security says duty-free allowances for food, alcohol and tobacco apply per person per day, and that if the total value of goods you bring exceeds CHF 150, VAT is payable in any case. Foodstuffs ordered abroad and delivered by post or courier follow different rules, and imports of animal products are allowed only from EU member states, Iceland, Northern Ireland and Norway.

The table of quantities, including the tobacco figures our card gives, did not appear in the text we could read, so we cannot re-confirm the 250 cigarettes figure or the age rule here. For the exact quantities and any penalties, the page points to the customs information office on +41 58 467 15 15. Check the table on the Swiss customs page before you travel.
switzerland.src: Source read: FOCBS (BAZG), Duty-free allowances: foodstuffs, alcohol and tobacco. The quantities table was not in the text read.

oman.h: What Oman Customs says about the tobacco and alcohol exemptions
p: Oman's General Directorate of Customs says up to 400 cigarettes are exempt from customs duty for a traveller. Non-Muslims may bring up to 2 litres of wine and 48 cans of beer, and the page states that Muslims are not allowed that exemption. The exemptions do not apply to someone, in the page's words, of the kind frequently passing the customs territory. The page mentions no minimum age.

Gifts must not exceed a total value of 300 riyals, and electronics and household appliances are allowed only in non-commercial quantities. Currency, bearer securities, banknotes or convertible precious metals and gemstones above 6,000 riyals must be declared. The page does not list penalties for exceeding the tobacco exemption.
oman.src: Source read: Oman Customs, Traveller services. No penalty for tobacco is stated.

qatar.h: What Qatar Customs says about the tobacco exemption
p: Qatar Customs says a traveller's tobacco exemption should not exceed 400 cigarettes, and that allowance can be swapped for 20 cigars, 300 g of pipe tobacco, 500 g of raw tobacco or 2 kg of shisha tobacco. The tobacco must also not exceed 3,000 riyals in value, and anything above the limit or the value cap is subject to customs duties on the excess.

The conditions are that the items are personal and in non-commercial quantities, that the traveller is not a frequent visitor to customs and does not trade in these goods, and that prohibitions and restrictions under the Customs Law still apply. The page does not mention alcohol or a minimum age, so ask Qatar Customs about both.
qatar.src: Source read: Qatar General Authority of Customs, Travelers declaration page (English). Alcohol and age are not on the page.

peru.h: What SUNAT says about tobacco in baggage
p: The Peruvian customs authority SUNAT says passengers over 18 may bring as exempt baggage 20 packs of cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 250 grams of loose or shredded smoking tobacco, with liquor limited to 3 litres. Personal-use goods and gifts are exempt if their combined value is up to US$500, and electrical devices, tools and professional equipment in that group are limited to one unit per type.
The page does not give a penalty for tobacco above the exemption or say what happens to the excess. Check SUNAT before you travel with more than the allowance.
peru.src: Source read: SUNAT, Equipaje y bienes (viajeros) (in Spanish). No tobacco penalty is stated.

serbia.h: What Serbian Customs says about the tobacco and alcohol allowance
p: Serbian Customs allows 50 cigarettes, or 25 cigarillos of up to 3 g each, or 10 cigars, or 50 g of tobacco, or a suitable combination. It also lists related products for personal use, such as e-cigarettes, vapes, nicotine pouches and hookah flavours, as allowed, and says snus is prohibited. The alcohol allowance is 1 litre of spirits or 1 litre of sparkling and liqueur wines, or a combination, plus 1 litre of other wines, and beer has no precise limit but must clearly be for personal use.

The page states no minimum age for the tobacco or alcohol allowances. Goods up to EUR 3,000 can be cleared at the border in the red channel with a single 10% customs rate plus VAT, usually 20%, and goods above that go through the regular procedure. Medicines are allowed for up to 15 days of regular therapy, and perfume is limited to one 50 ml bottle and one 25 ml toilet water. Non-residents can get a VAT refund on unused goods worth at least 6,000 dinars if exported within three months.
serbia.src: Source read: Carina.rs, FAQ for tourists (English). No age rule or penalty for tobacco is stated.

seychelles.h: What Seychelles Revenue Commission says about duty-free allowances
p: The Seychelles Revenue Commission says passengers aged 18 and over may bring 250 g of tobacco products, or 200 cigarettes, which covers cigars, cheroots, snuff and smoking and chewing tobacco. The alcohol allowance is up to 2 litres of drinks at or below 16% alcohol, such as beer, wine and sparkling wine, and up to 2 litres of drinks above 16%, such as whisky, rum, gin and distilled liqueurs.

Other goods are allowed up to SCR 15,000, including one electronic item, and perfume up to 200 ml. Duty-free goods must be for personal use only. Passengers who exceed their allowance pay the applicable taxes on arrival, and failing to declare excess goods is a serious offence that can lead to heavy fines, seizure and possible prosecution. If you are unsure, use the red channel. The page does not state the fine amounts.
seychelles.src: Source read: Seychelles Revenue Commission, Customs and Excises. Fine amounts are not on the page.

philippines.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in the Philippines
p: The Travel Doc customs page for the Philippines allows travellers aged 18 and over 2 reams of tobacco, 50 cigars or 250 g of pipe tobacco.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
philippines.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for the Philippines (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

russia.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in Russia
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Russia allows travellers aged 18 and over one of: 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars or 250 g of loose tobacco, or a mix totalling up to 250 g.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
russia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Russia (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

saudi-arabia.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in Saudi Arabia
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Saudi Arabia lists 200 cigarettes or 25 cigars as free to import, plus a separate hookah tobacco allowance of 500 g. It states no age limit.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
saudi-arabia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Saudi Arabia (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.
link: Travel Doc: Saudi Arabia customs information

south-africa.h: What SARS says about the duty-free tobacco allowance
p: The South African Revenue Service guide on duty-free allowances for travellers says a traveller may import free of duty and tax 200 cigarettes, 20 cigars, and a combined 250 g of pipe and cigarette tobacco, along with 2 litres of wine, 1 litre of other alcoholic drinks including beer, 250 ml of eau de toilette and 50 ml of perfume. The tobacco and alcohol allowances are not available to anyone under 18, and crew members, including the master or pilot, are not entitled to any duty-free consumables.

Consumables above the limits cannot be claimed under the duty-free allowance, and full duty and VAT must be paid on the excess. The allowance may be used once per person in a 30-day cycle after an absence of more than 48 hours. On top of the duty-free allowance, a flat rate allowance lets you bring additional goods up to R20,000 at a rate of 20%, with VAT exempted, and crew are limited to R2,000. The guide does not describe penalties for undeclared tobacco.
south-africa.src: Source read: SARS, SC-PA-01-03 Duty-free allowances for travellers (external guide, PDF). Penalties are not in the part read.

united-arab-emirates.h: What the UAE government portal says about the tobacco allowance
p: The official UAE government portal says a traveller may bring 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 500 g of tobacco, including pipe tobacco, tumbak and hookah molasses, along with up to 4 litres of alcoholic drinks or 2 cartons of beer of 24 cans each, with no can above 355 ml. Gifts, perfumes and personal luggage together must not exceed AED 3,000, must be limited in quantity and not commercial, and the traveller must not be a frequent carrier of goods or crew.

Customs duty plus VAT applies to quantities and values above these limits. The page does not state a rate for the excess, so the 100% figure sometimes quoted is not confirmed here. It also sets no minimum age for tobacco, alcohol or gifts, so check the age rule with UAE customs and the rules of the emirate where you land, because alcohol rules differ between emirates.
united-arab-emirates.src: Source read: u.ae, Customs clearance. The duty rate on the excess and the age rule are not on the page.

south-korea.h: What Korea Customs says about tobacco and the duty-free allowance
p: The Korea Customs Service page on duty-free allowances sets a total of US$800 in taxable value, with tobacco treated separately: 200 cigarette sticks, or e-cigarette or liquid nicotine up to 20 ml with nicotine under 1%. Liquor has its own allowance of up to 2 litres together with US$400, outside the US$800 limit, and perfume is 100 ml. The page does not mention cigars or loose tobacco. Minors under 19, counted by year of birth, are not given the tax exemption for liquor and cigarettes.

If you declare goods above the allowances yourself, you get a 30% reduction from the standard customs duty. Undeclared goods found later face an additional tax of 40% above the regular tax, or 60% if caught two or more times within 2 years. Agricultural, livestock and fishery products have separate limits of 5 kg per item, 40 kg in total and 100,000 won in value.
south-korea.src: Source read: Korea Customs Service, duty-free allowance page (English). Cigars and loose tobacco are not on it.

vietnam.h: What Vietnam Law Magazine says about the tobacco allowance
p: Vietnam Law Magazine, an English-language legal publication, reports in an article dated 16 September 2026 that under Decree 273/2026/ND-CP, Article 5, travellers entering Vietnam may bring 200 cigarettes, or 250 grams of shredded tobacco, or 20 cigars, and each is a separate option, not a combined limit. The alcohol and tobacco allowances do not apply to anyone under 18.

For alcohol the article says the 1.5-litre allowance covers drinks with 20% or more alcohol, below 20% the limit is 2 litres, and other spirits and beer are capped at 3 litres, with an unopened container possibly still exempt if the excess is no more than 1 litre. Other goods can be duty-exempt if their total customs value is no more than VND 10 million. The article gives no effective date for the decree and no penalties. It is a magazine, not a Vietnamese authority, which is why the card is marked unofficial.
vietnam.src: Source read: Vietnam Law Magazine, article of 16 September 2026. This is an unofficial source.

jordan.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about tobacco in Jordan
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Jordan allows travellers aged 18 and over 200 cigarettes.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
jordan.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Jordan (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

portugal.h: What the Portuguese tax authority adds on tobacco
p: The Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira travellers guide (February 2026) gives travellers from non-EU countries 200 cigarettes, or 100 cigarillos (cigars of 3 g or less each), or 50 cigars, or 250 g of smoking tobacco, or a proportional mix of these products.

The guide also lists separate duty-free quantities for snuff, chewing tobacco, heated tobacco, e-cigarette liquid and nicotine pouches; this page does not quote them because the PDF table is hard to read in text form, so check the guide itself. Travellers under 17 from non-EU countries get no tobacco or alcohol allowance.
faq: How many cigarettes can I bring into Portugal from outside the EU?
The February 2026 guide from the Portuguese tax and customs authority allows 200 cigarettes, or an equivalent amount of other tobacco products, for travellers from non-EU countries.
Can a 16-year-old bring tobacco into Portugal?
No. The guide says travellers under 17 from non-EU countries get no allowance for tobacco products or alcoholic drinks.
portugal.src: Source read 16 November 2026: Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (portaldasfinancas.gov.pt), Guia para Viajantes, February 2026 (PDF, in Portuguese).

slovakia.h: What the Slovak Financial Administration says about tobacco in luggage
p: The Slovak Financial Administration says travellers aged 17 or over may carry tobacco in their luggage, for non-commercial and occasional use, within two sets of limits. By air, per person, it is 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco, plus ten consumer packs of smokeless tobacco. By other transport it is 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of smoking tobacco, plus two consumer packs of smokeless tobacco. Products can be mixed if the shares of each limit add up to no more than 100%, for example 60 cigarillos by air, which is 60%, plus 20 cigars, which is 40%.

For alcohol the page allows up to 1 litre of spirits over 22% or 2 litres of weaker spirits, 2 litres of sparkling wine, 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, again with a 100% combination rule. The value limits for the VAT and customs exemption are EUR 430 by air, EUR 300 by other transport and EUR 150 for anyone under 15. Excess quantities are taxed in Slovakia. The page describes no penalties, so ask the Financial Administration about sanctions.
slovakia.src: Source read: Finančná správa, Oslobodenie od cla, DPH a SPD (in Slovak). No penalties are stated.

finland.h: What the Finnish Customs leaflet says about tobacco
p: The leaflet gives travellers from outside the EU 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 100 cigarillos (3 g or less each), or 250 g of roll-your-own or pipe tobacco, or a proportional mix. It also allows up to 10 ml of nicotine liquid for e-cigarettes. Nobody under 18 may bring in tobacco or nicotine liquid.

Even if you pay duty, you may not bring more than the allowance when the packs lack the health warnings required in Finnish and Swedish. Snus, chewing tobacco and snuff are limited to 1,000 g per day and only for your own use. Arriving from outside the EEA by means other than air, visitors living outside the EEA can bring tobacco only on stays over 72 hours. The leaflet is from 2021.
faq: How many cigarettes can I bring into Finland from outside the EU?
