Finnish Customs’ 2021 leaflet allows 200 cigarettes, or an equivalent amount of other tobacco products, tax-free for travellers from outside the EU. Check tulli.fi for current rules.
finland.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Finnish Customs leaflet "Customs advice for travellers" (6/2021), read as a copy hosted by expat-finland.com. The tulli.fi pages could not be opened. The leaflet is from 2021 and says to check tulli.fi for current rules.

greece.h: What the Greek customs authority (AADE) says about tobacco
p: AADE gives the allowance for travellers arriving from outside the EU by how you travel. By air: 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos (cigars up to 3 g each), 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco, or a proportional mix. By every other means of transport, which includes ships: only 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of smoking tobacco, or a proportional mix. This lower limit also covers sea arrivals, which is the point some travel sites get wrong. Travellers under 17 get no allowance for tobacco or spirits.

New to this page: electronic cigarettes, heated tobacco products and nicotine pouches carried in person from a third country for your own use are exempt from excise duty, up to 20 ml of e-cigarette liquid (or 2 vials of 10 ml), 200 nicotine pouches (10 packs of 20), or 200 heated-tobacco sticks with or without tobacco (10 packs of 20). Customs judge own use from your trade status, how the goods travel, documents, the nature and the quantity.
greece.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Greek Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE), "Frequently asked questions - answers on exemptions for travellers from third countries", version 2.0 of 3 April 2026 (aade.gr, in Greek, translated by us).
link: AADE: Tax relief for third-country travellers (FAQ PDF, Greek)

lithuania.h: What Lithuanian Customs says about tobacco
p: Lithuanian Customs says one person over 17 arriving from outside the EU may bring duty-free, by air: 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos (cigars up to 3 g each), 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco, plus 200 heated-tobacco units and 50 ml of e-cigarette liquid. By any other transport, and for crew and border-zone residents: 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g, plus 40 heated-tobacco units and 20 ml of liquid.
Cigarettes and tobacco from Russia and Belarus are banned from import into Lithuania, and from 3 June 2024 so are many agricultural goods from those countries.

From another EU country, Hinterland Travel (unofficial) lists own-use amounts that customs does not treat as trade: 800 cigarettes, 400 cigarillos, 200 cigars or 1 kg of smoking tobacco, with excise already paid there. Above that you may be asked to prove personal use.
lithuania.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Lithuanian Customs (Lietuvos Respublikos muitine), "Coming from third countries" (muitine.lrv.lt, English; read from an archived copy because the live site refuses our reader). EU-travel figures from Hinterland Travel (unofficial, read 23 November 2026).
link: Lithuanian Customs: coming from third countries

malta.h: What the Maltese tax and customs administration says about tobacco
p: The Malta Tax and Customs Administration page on travellers' allowances says that from a non-EU country you may bring tobacco for your own use, if you are at least 17, free of import duty, excise and VAT: 200 cigarettes, or 100 cigarillos (cigars of at most 3 grams each), or 50 cigars, or 250 g of smoking tobacco, or a mix of them in proportion.

For tobacco bought in another EU country, excise is paid where it was bought. The page gives guide levels, not hard limits: 800 cigarettes, 400 cigarillos, 200 cigars or 1 kg of smoking tobacco. Customs decide whether it is for your own use by looking at who you are, why you hold it, where it was found and how you travel, any papers, the kind of goods and the quantity.

Malta International Airport's customs page adds that the allowance does not apply under 17, and that smokeless tobacco (chewing tobacco, heets, snus, snuff), unbranded tobacco and flavoured tobacco are on the prohibited or restricted list.
malta.src: Source read on 22 November 2026: Malta Tax and Customs Administration (mtca.gov.mt), Travellers Allowances on Accompanied Goods from Non-EU or EU Countries. Also read 23 November 2026: Malta International Airport, Customs page (the airport operator).

poland.h: What the Polish Ministry of Finance says about tobacco
p: From outside the EU, the Polish customs-duty exemption for tobacco applies from age 17. By air or sea: 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of tobacco. By land or other routes: only 40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g. This is the 40-cigarette land figure, not 50.

From another EU country, tobacco with excise paid there is allowed for own use up to 800 cigarettes, 400 cigarillos, 200 cigars or 1 kg of smoking tobacco before customs treats it as commercial. Border-zone residents, border-zone workers and crew of vehicles crossing the EU border have their own lower alcohol limits.

The tax administration's (KAS) travellers' guide, as summarised by Dziennik Gazeta Prawna on 22 June 2024, says you may mix tobacco products as long as the shares of each limit add up to no more than 100%. A traveller arriving by plane can bring 100 cigarettes (50% of the limit) and 25 cigars (50%). The same guide puts the general goods limit at 430 euros by air or sea and 300 euros by other transport, and says tobacco, alcohol, medicines and fuel in the tank or a can do not count towards that value limit.
poland.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Polish Ministry of Finance, podatki.gov.pl, "Towary przywożone przez podróżnych zwolnione z opłat" (published and updated 15 December 2025). Dziennik Gazeta Prawna, 22 June 2024, summary of the KAS travellers' guide (read 24 November 2026; the guide itself was not opened).
link: Polish Ministry of Finance: goods carried by travellers exempt from charges

romania.h: What TAROM tells passengers about tobacco in Romania
p: TAROM's customs page says passengers should declare cigarettes above two cartons, 200 pieces, when entering or leaving Romania.

The Travel Doc customs page we read earlier gives travellers aged 18 and over from outside the EU 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of smoking tobacco, or a proportional mix. Neither page is the customs authority's, so confirm with Romanian customs.

Press reports of 6 to 8 August 2026 describe Joint Order No. 1,613/956/2026 of ANAF and the Romanian Customs Authority, published in the Official Gazette on 6 August. It sets reference periods over which tobacco and alcohol that one person brings from another EU country are added together: 40 days for tobacco products and one year for alcohol, within the Fiscal Code limits of 800 cigarettes, 400 cigarillos up to 3 g each, 200 cigars and 1 kg of smoking tobacco. The order also creates an electronic register in which customs records each finding on a form signed by the officer and the person; a copy can be requested within seven days. Authorities use it to check that the trips are occasional and for own use, a condition from Emergency Ordinance 68/2025. Press says exceeding the limits when goods no longer count as own use can bring fines of 20,000 to 100,000 lei and confiscation.
romania.src: Unofficial source, read 22 November 2026: TAROM, the Romanian national airline, page "Customs clearance". It is not the customs authority's page, whose site could not be read. The Travel Doc page (infopages.traveldoc.aero) is undated and names no publisher. Adevarul.ro (8 August 2026), a news report on the joint order, read 24 November 2026; we did not read the order text itself.

ukraine.h: What the Customs Code of Ukraine says about tobacco
p: The Customs Code of Ukraine (zakon.rada.gov.ua, articles 374 and 376, read on 23 and 24 November 2026 from an archived copy of the 2025 text) allows an adult passenger aged 18 or over one of 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars or 250 g of tobacco, or a mix that stays within 250 g in total. Anyone under 18 may not bring tobacco in.

The code keeps excise goods out of the general duty-free allowance of goods worth up to 1,000 euro in hand or accompanied baggage, so tobacco never counts towards that value. If you were away from Ukraine for less than 24 hours, tobacco and alcohol are taxed whatever the quantity. The code does not name e-cigarettes.
ukraine.src: Source read: Customs Code of Ukraine (zakon.rada.gov.ua), articles 374 and 376, from an archived copy of the 2025 text.
link: Customs Code of Ukraine: articles 374 and 376

panama.h: Tobacco in Panama: the card, an unofficial source and the general rule
p: We have no card figure for Panama because we found no readable official page for it.

The official page could not be re-opened, and the UK government's travel advice for Panama, which we also read, says nothing about tobacco. So this section applies the general rule most countries follow: customs services usually count cigarettes, cigars and loose tobacco against one shared allowance, so mixing products does not add up to more. We have no figure for Panama, so ask the Panamanian customs authority before you travel.
panama.src: Official page not re-opened; the UK government (FCDO) advice read on 16 November 2026 does not cover tobacco. Global rule applied, unofficial.

lebanon.h: What Lebanese Customs says about tobacco
p: The Lebanese Customs traveller's guide allows people arriving in Lebanon, aged 18 and over, one of: 800 cigarettes, 1,000 g of pipe tobacco, 50 cigars, 50 cigarillos or 1,000 g of tobacco for water pipes. Travellers under 18 get no tobacco allowance.

Visitors who come for the summer season (1 June to 31 October) may also bring 800 cigarettes or 1,000 g of tobacco duty-free each. Larger non-commercial quantities pay the normal customs duty. Cigarillos are 50 in the official guide, not the 100 given by some other sites.
lebanon.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Lebanese Customs Administration, "Traveller's guide" (customs.gov.lb, in Arabic, translated by us; copyright 2019 on the site).

austria.h: What the Austrian Ministry of Finance adds
p: The Austrian Ministry of Finance (BMF) lets travellers aged 17 or over bring 1 litre of spirits above 22% vol. (or undenatured ethyl alcohol of 80% vol. or more) or 2 litres of drinks of 22% vol. or less, and the two can be mixed proportionally. On top of that come 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer.

Alcohol is separate from the other-goods value limit of EUR 430 by air or EUR 300 otherwise (EUR 150 under 15). You must file a customs declaration if you exceed the alcohol, wine or beer allowances, bring goods that are not for personal use, or bring anything banned or restricted. Entering through another EU country may bring that country's own rules.
austria.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Austrian Ministry of Finance, Freimengen und Freigrenze (bmf.gv.at). The page carries no date.
link: Austrian Ministry of Finance: Freimengen und Freigrenze

p: Czech Customs allows 1 litre of spirits above 22% vol. (or undenatured alcohol of at least 80% vol.) and 2 litres of drinks up to 22% vol., and the two can be combined if their shares total no more than 100%: for example 0.5 litre of spirits plus 1 litre of drinks up to 22% vol. Separately you may bring 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer.

The exemption does not apply to travellers under 17. Alcohol is not counted toward the value limits, which are EUR 430 for air travel, EUR 300 for recreational or sports flying and EUR 200 for under-15s by air. The page was published on 13 May 2025.
czechia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Czech Customs Administration, information for travellers from third countries (celnisprava.gov.cz), published 13 May 2025.
link: Czech Customs Administration: information for travellers from third countries

p: Croatian Customs gives the same alcohol quantities for air, sea and other transport from a third country: 1 litre of spirits above 22% vol. (or undenatured alcohol of 80% or more), up to 2 litres of drinks of 22% or less, 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. Excise exemptions may not apply to travellers under 17.

For goods bought with duty paid in another EU state, the personal-use guide quantities are 10 litres of spirits, 20 litres of drinks between 1.2% and 22%, 90 litres of wine (no more than 60 litres sparkling) and 110 litres of beer. Above those, goods must be returned abroad. The page shows no update date; only the footer reads 2026.
croatia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Croatian Customs Administration, relief from duties for passengers (carina.gov.hr). The page shows no update date.
link: Croatian Customs Administration: relief from duties for passengers

p: The Cyprus Customs and Excise Department allows 1 litre of spirits above 22% (or undenatured ethyl alcohol of 80% or more) or 2 litres of drinks of 22% or less, plus 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. Travellers under 17 get no relief on alcohol.

Crew members have 0.25 litre of spirits, 0.5 litre of weaker drinks, 1 litre of still wine and 3 litres of beer. Other goods are relieved up to EUR 430 per person (EUR 175 under 15). Declare in the red channel at Larnaca, Paphos or Limassol if you exceed any allowance. The page was last updated on 5 February 2020.
cyprus.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Cyprus Customs and Excise Department, general allowances (mof.gov.cy). Last updated 5 February 2020.
link: Cyprus Customs and Excise Department: general allowances

p: German Customs (zoll.de) allows importers aged 17 or over 1 litre of spirits above 22% vol. (or undenatured ethyl alcohol of at least 80% vol.) or 2 litres of drinks of 22% vol. or less, or a proportional mix, and separately 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. Duty-free purchases when you enter from a non-EU country count towards these quantities together with everything else you bought there.

Allowances may be used only once per trip, and the limits of several travellers cannot be pooled. For alcohol bought in another EU country, the guide quantities are 10 litres of spirits, 20 litres of intermediate products such as sherry or port, 60 litres of sparkling wine and 110 litres of beer; there is no tax guide quantity for still wine. They apply only if you carry the goods yourself. Duty-free shop purchases made inside the EU must always be declared and carry no allowance. Above the limits the goods are presumed commercial unless you credibly show personal use.
germany.src: Sources read 15 November 2026: zoll.de, Reisefreimengen and Genussmittel pages. Neither page shows a date.

slovenia.h: What the Slovenian Financial Administration adds
p: FURS allows 1 litre of alcohol above 22% vol. (or undenatured alcohol of 80% vol. or more) or 2 litres of alcohol not exceeding 22% vol., or a proportional mix, plus 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. Travellers under 17 are not entitled to relief for alcohol.

The relief covers non-commercial goods in personal luggage imported occasionally for personal or family use or as presents. The page does not say whether the proportional rule extends to the wine and beer allowances, and it is dated 23 September 2020.
slovenia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Slovenian Financial Administration, Import of alcoholic beverages and tobacco products (fu.gov.si), refreshed 23 September 2020.
link: Slovenian Financial Administration: import of alcoholic beverages and tobacco products

p: Dutch Customs allows travellers aged 17 or older from a non-EU country 16 litres of beer, 4 litres of still wine (sparkling wine is not included in that figure) and either 1 litre of strong spirits or 2 litres of lighter drinks such as liqueur or sparkling wine. If you take some of both, you take proportionally less of the other: 0.5 litre of spirits plus 1 litre of sparkling wine is allowed, but 1 litre of spirits plus 1 litre of liqueur is not.

From another EU country or Northern Ireland the personal-use quantities are 110 litres of beer, 90 litres of wine (up to 60 litres sparkling), 20 litres of light liqueur and 10 litres of strong spirits. Above the allowance you must declare and pay duty, excise and VAT, and without receipts or other proof of personal use the drinks can be seized. Crew from non-EU countries may bring 1 litre of spirits, 2 litres of still wine and 8 litres of beer. Page updated 29 June 2026.
netherlands.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Dutch Customs (douane.nl), bringing drinks from abroad, updated 29 June 2026.
link: Dutch Customs: bringing drinks from abroad

denmark.h: What the Danish Customs Agency adds
p: Toldstyrelsen splits Danish alcohol allowances by type: 1 litre of spirits above 22% (including drinks to which alcohol has been added), 2 litres of fortified wine (22% or less, such as port, sherry or madeira) or sparkling wine such as champagne, 4 litres of table wine (including cider-based wine) and 16 litres of beer (including beer-based cider). You must be 17.

The page links the categories with 'and', which suggests they are cumulative, though it does not say so explicitly. Alcohol does not count toward the DKK 3,250 (plane or ship) or DKK 2,250 (other transport) threshold for other goods; the page's example is a DKK 1,500 whisky bought on a flight that leaves room for other goods up to DKK 3,250.
denmark.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Danish Customs Agency (toldst.dk), customs rules when travelling to countries outside the EU.
link: Danish Customs Agency: travelling outside the EU

p: Irish Revenue allows 1 litre of spirits or 2 litres of drinks of no more than 22% alcohol (port, sherry, sparkling wine, some liqueurs), plus 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. The spirits and lighter-drink allowances can be split, for example 0.5 litre of spirits with 1 litre of port; the page does not say whether wine or beer can be mixed with them.

Crew on transport have 0.35 litre of spirits, 0.5 litre of weaker drinks, 0.75 litre of still wine and 4 litres of beer. Alcohol and tobacco are separate from the EUR 430 general goods limit (EUR 215 under 15), and duty-free goods bought when leaving Ireland count toward that general limit. Customs duty, excise and VAT are charged above the allowances. Page dated 22 December 2025.
ireland.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Irish Revenue (revenue.ie), duty-free allowances from outside the EU, dated 22 December 2025.
link: Irish Revenue: duty-free allowances from outside the EU

italy.h: What the Italian Customs and Monopolies Agency adds
p: Italy's customs agency, in its July 2025 traveller guide, allows 1 litre of alcohol above 22% vol. (or undenatured ethyl alcohol of 80% vol. or more) or 2 litres of drinks of 22% vol. or less, plus 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. Each quantity counts as 100%, and any combination is fine if the percentages add up to no more than 100%. Travellers under 17 are excluded.

Alcohol is not counted in the value limit of EUR 300 (EUR 430 by air or sea, EUR 150 under 15). Goods above the allowance can be left in customs custody for 90 days while formalities are completed; after that they are declared abandoned and pass to the state. For trips within the EU, the guide gives indicative thresholds such as 10 litres of spirits and 110 litres of beer.
italy.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Agenzia delle Dogane e dei Monopoli, Carta doganale del viaggiatore (July 2025 edition).
link: Italian Customs and Monopolies Agency: Carta doganale del viaggiatore

p: Swedish Customs requires you to be at least 20 years old to bring alcohol and to carry it yourself for your or your family's personal use. From outside the EU (which also covers Åland, the Canary Islands and duty-free shops) the allowance is duty-free if you were abroad at least 20 hours or arrive on a commercial flight: 1 litre of spirits or 2 litres of fortified wine (including sparkling), 4 litres of wine and 16 litres of beer, mixed within each category.

Anything above must be declared in the red lane. Swedish Customs gives the charge per litre: spirits SEK 4 customs duty plus SEK 267 excise, fortified wine SEK 2 plus SEK 92, wine SEK 1 plus SEK 41, and beer SEK 3 plus SEK 23. From another EU country there are no fees if you carry the alcohol yourself for personal use; the guideline amounts are 10 litres of spirits, 20 of fortified wine, 90 of wine (60 sparkling) and 110 of beer, but these are not a hard limit and you may be asked to prove personal use, for example with documents for a party or wedding. Alcohol judged not to be for personal use can be seized. Page updated 10 September 2026.
sweden.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Swedish Customs (tullverket.se), buying alcohol when travelling, updated 10 September 2026.
link: Swedish Customs: buying alcohol when travelling

estonia.h: What the Estonian Tax and Customs Board adds
p: EMTA allows travellers aged 18 or over, on their first entry in a calendar month, up to 4 litres of wine (not sparkling or liqueur wine), 16 litres of beer and either 2 litres of drinks up to 22% alcohol (including sparkling and liqueur wine) or 1 litre of drinks over 22%. Combinations count as percentages: 1.5 litres at up to 22% plus 0.25 litre over 22% makes 100%.

On a second entry in a month EMTA may grant an extra exemption if you prove the import was occasional; air, train and sea travellers are not limited by crossing frequency. Spirits above 22% may be brought in only if they were not produced in Russia and are not brought from Russia, and alcohol from Russia is limited to 16 litres of beer, 4 litres of wine and 2 litres of light alcohol. Value limits for other goods are EUR 300, or EUR 430 by air or sea. Page updated 27 October 2026.
estonia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Estonian Tax and Customs Board (emta.ee), From a third country to Estonia, updated 27 October 2026.
link: Estonian Tax and Customs Board: from a third country to Estonia

latvia.h: What Latvia's State Revenue Service adds
p: Latvia's State Revenue Service (VID) allows 1 litre of drinks above 22% alcohol (or undenatured ethyl alcohol of 80% or more), 2 litres of drinks up to 22% (including sparkling, fortified and fruit or berry wines, but not still wine or beer), 4 litres of still wine made only from grapes and 16 litres of beer. Combinations of the first two are fine if the percentages total no more than 100%. Individuals under 18 have no import allowance for alcohol.

EU sanctions ban spirit drinks, including whisky, vodka, rum, gin and liqueurs, from Russia and Belarus; naturally fermented wine and beer without artificial flavours or additives are excepted. Use the red channel for goods above the limits. At the land border with Russia or Belarus a Statement on the Transport of Excise Goods is required in certain cases, including entering Latvia more than once per 30 days. Undeclared goods above the limits can bring a fine of up to 400 fine units (EUR 2,000). Page updated 22 April 2025.
latvia.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Latvian State Revenue Service (vid.gov.lv), Excise goods, updated 22 April 2025.
link: Latvian State Revenue Service: excise goods

p: Luxembourg Customs allows 1 litre of spirits above 22% vol. (or pure ethyl alcohol of 80% or more) or 2 litres of drinks of 22% or less, on top of 4 litres of still wine and up to 16 litres of beer, which the page says count only for VAT and excise purposes. Travellers under 17 cannot bring alcohol or tobacco duty-free.

Other goods are limited by value (EUR 430 by air or sea, EUR 300 for other travellers, EUR 175 for under-15s), and allowances cannot be pooled between people for one item. Goods carried together in one vehicle that form a single multi-part item count as one item whatever the number of invoices. You must declare the goods to the customs office on entry, and an item over the allowance is taxed on its full value with no deduction. Page updated 30 July 2026.
luxembourg.src: Source read 15 November 2026: Luxembourg Customs (douanes.public.lu), arriving from a country outside the EU, updated 30 July 2026.
link: Luxembourg Customs: arriving from a country outside the EU

brazil.h: What the Brazilian Federal Revenue says about alcohol in baggage
p: The Brazilian Federal Revenue (Receita Federal) says a traveller may bring up to 12 litres of alcoholic drinks in total in baggage, by air, sea or land. Over the limit, the drinks are treated as ordinary baggage without the tax exemption. The arrival Free Shop has its own limit: at a land border up to 12 litres, and at a port or airport up to 24 units, with no more than 12 units of any one type of drink.

Travellers under 18 cannot buy alcohol at the Free Shop, even when accompanied, and alcohol cannot be part of the baggage of a child or teenager even with a legal guardian. The page does not mention wine or beer separately, so the rules apply to alcoholic drinks in general. Purchases above the extra arrival quota are taxed under the special RTE regime, which the page does not explain, and it gives no fine for exceeding the limit.
brazil.src: Source read: Receita Federal, Cota de isenção, duty free e bagagem tributável (in Portuguese). The RTE regime and fines are not explained on the page.

canada.h: What the Canada Border Services Agency says about alcohol limits
p: The Canada Border Services Agency says non-residents and temporary residents may bring 1.5 litres of wine, or 1.14 litres of spirits, or 1.14 litres of wine and spirits combined, or 8.5 litres of beer or ale. The minimum age is 18 if you enter through Alberta, Manitoba or Quebec, and 19 elsewhere. Our card says you must meet the drinking age of the province where you arrive, and the page fixes it at those two figures.

The page does not call alcohol within these limits duty-free: it says duties and taxes could apply and that you should be ready to pay them on any declared amount. Each gift under CAD 60 is exempt from duties and taxes, but tobacco, vaping products and alcohol cannot count as exempt gifts. Amounts above the limits may need a permit from the provincial or territorial authority. The page states no penalty for undeclared alcohol.
canada.src: Source read: CBSA, What can I bring: alcohol and tobacco for non-residents. No penalty for undeclared alcohol is stated.

chile.h: What Chilean Customs says about the alcohol allowance
p: The Chilean customs service says the duty- and tax-free baggage allowance for each adult traveller includes 2,500 cubic centimetres of alcoholic drinks, next to 400 cigarettes, 500 grams of pipe tobacco and 50 cigars. The page does not define the adult age for the baggage rule, but for Duty Free purchases, buyers of cigarettes and alcohol must be over 18.

Duty Free shop goods are exempt from duties and internal taxes up to US$675 if non-commercial, must be in sealed packaging and may not be opened before clearing customs. Personal imports without a customs agent are allowed up to US$1,500, with 6% duty and 19% VAT. We read the first 100,000 characters of a long page, and the penalty for exceeding the alcohol allowance is not in the part read.
chile.src: Source read: Aduanas de Chile, Preguntas frecuentes viajero y turista (in Spanish), first 100,000 characters.

dominican-republic.h: What the Dominican customs traveller manual says about alcohol
p: The Dominican customs traveller manual says adult passengers may bring up to 5 litres of alcoholic drinks duty-free, whether wine, beer, rum, whisky or another liquor. The page sets the adult threshold only through the word adult and gives no numeric age, so ask Customs what age applies.

Gifts up to US$500 are allowed once every three months, and each traveller may bring one laptop and one tablet duty-free. Items beyond the allowances are subject to taxes, and the manual lists drugs, psychotropic substances and firearms as prohibited. It does not say what happens to alcohol above 5 litres beyond the tax and gives no fine.
dominican-republic.src: Source read: DGA, Manual del Viajero (in Spanish). No numeric age or fine is stated.

cambodia.h: What the Cambodia Airports customs page says about alcohol
p: The customs and excise page of Cambodia Airports says an arriving passenger may bring up to 2 litres of alcohol, and passengers under 18 may not bring alcohol or tobacco. Our card adds that the Ministry of Tourism's site also gives 2 litres. The same page lists 200 cigarettes, 350 ml of perfume and cosmetics and a reasonable quantity of travel items.

Goods worth US$100 or more are subject to duties and taxes, and a false declaration or using the green channel to avoid declaring dutiable goods can lead to fines or prosecution. The page is an airport operator's summary, not the Cambodian customs department, which is why the card is marked unofficial.
cambodia.src: Source read: Cambodia Airports, Customs and excise. This is an airport operator page and an unofficial source.

cuba.h: What the Cuban tourism portal says about alcohol
p: The Cuban tourism portal lists, per adult, up to 2,500 cc of alcoholic drinks among the personal effects a traveller may bring, next to 400 cigarettes, 500 g of pipe tobacco and 50 Cuban cigars. It says quantities above those listed for each item are not treated as personal effects and are subject to the rules for imported goods, and that under the weight and value method, 25 kg of goods count as personal effects and pay no customs duty.

The page does not give an age limit or a penalty. It is a tourism portal, not Cuban Customs, which is why the card is marked unofficial, and Cuban Customs' own site would not open securely for us earlier. Check Cuban Customs before you travel.
cuba.src: Source read: cuba.travel, Accessories for traveling. This is a tourism portal and an unofficial source.

argentina.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Argentina
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Argentina allows 2 litres of alcohol, or 1 litre for visitors and returning residents coming from Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay or Uruguay. Travellers under 18 get half of these amounts.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
argentina.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Argentina (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

australia.h: What Sydney Airport says about alcohol
p: Sydney Airport’s information sheet on duty-free allowances for arriving passengers says each adult (18 or over) can bring in 2.25 litres of liquor, wine or champagne duty-free. It adds that duty and tax are payable on all items of that type, not only on the amount above the limit, if the allowance is exceeded.

The sheet lists the alcohol allowance for adults only, so we do not show an allowance for travellers under 18. It shows no update date. Because this is an airport operator and not the Australian Border Force, treat it as a guide and confirm on the Border Force website before you fly.
australia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Sydney Airport, duty-free allowances for arriving passengers (airport operator page, undated). The Australian Border Force page could not be opened.
link: Sydney Airport: duty-free allowances for arriving passengers

bahrain.h: What Bahrain Customs says about alcohol
p: Bahrain Customs Affairs, on its page "Duty Free Allowances" (read from an archived copy on 24 November 2026), exempts 3 litres of alcoholic beverages and 12 cans of beer carried by a traveller, within the same list as BD 300 of personal goods and gifts.

The conditions on that page: alcohol and tobacco must be in the possession of someone aged 18 or over; goods must be personal and not commercial; the traveller must not be a frequent flyer who brings goods in regularly; and flight crew follow a separate mechanism. Customs may keep dutiable goods for up to three months at the traveller's request. The page names no religion-based rule and no penalty, and an older undated third-party page that gave 1 litre of spirits and 6 cans does not match it.
bahrain.src: Source read: Bahrain Customs Affairs, Duty Free Allowances (customs.gov.bh), read from an archived copy on 24 November 2026.
link: Bahrain Customs Affairs: Duty Free Allowances

belgium.h: What Brussels Airport says about alcohol
p: Brussels Airport's customs page gives travellers from outside the EU up to 1 litre of spirits or 2 litres of wine at the green exit. The red exit is for anyone above the limits, and a check is always possible.

Other goods, perfume included, must total under 430 euros, and cash or gold of 10,000 euros or more also goes through the red exit. Different limits apply from another EU country, so confirm with Belgian customs.
belgium.src: Reliable unofficial source, read 22 November 2026: Brussels Airport customs page. It is the airport operator's page, not Belgian customs, which it points to for full details.

bulgaria.h: What the Bulgarian Customs Agency says about alcohol
p: The Bulgarian Customs Agency allows travellers over 17 years of age arriving from a third country 1 litre of spirits above 22% vol (or undenatured ethyl alcohol of 80% vol or more) or 2 litres of drinks up to 22% vol, plus 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. The two spirit categories can be mixed while the used percentages stay within 100%; wine and beer are separate. The agency gives the age as over 17, not 18.

Crew have a smaller allowance: 1 litre of strong spirits or 1 litre of weaker drinks, plus 2 litres of still wine and 4 litres of beer. Other goods, including perfumes, coffee and tea, are free up to 430 euros for air and sea travellers, 300 euros for others and 150 euros for children; a single item cannot be split to fit. Medicines are free in the quantity and type needed for personal use, and a vehicle may bring its standard tank plus 10 litres of fuel in a portable container.
bulgaria.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Bulgarian Customs Agency, "Brief summary of the monetary thresholds and quantitative limits for goods contained in the personal luggage of travellers coming from third countries and territories" (customs.bg, English page; read from an archived copy because the live site refused our reader).
link: Bulgarian Customs Agency: allowances for travellers from third countries

china.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in China
p: The Travel Doc customs page for China allows travellers aged 16 and over up to 1.5 litres of alcohol of 12% or higher.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
china.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for China (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

colombia.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Colombia
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Colombia allows travellers aged 18 and over up to 10 units of alcoholic drinks, with a total value not above USD 2,000.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
colombia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Colombia (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

costa-rica.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Costa Rica
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Costa Rica lists a free allowance of 5 litres of alcohol, limited to travellers aged 18 and over.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
costa-rica.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Costa Rica (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.
link: Travel Doc: Costa Rica customs information

egypt.h: What the Egyptian Customs Authority says about alcohol for tourists
p: The Egyptian Customs Authority page for tourists and transit passengers says a tourist may bring one litre of spirits, together with one carton of cigarettes, 25 cigars or 200 g of tobacco, and duties and taxes apply to anything above. Residents have the same allowance. The page does not say the quantity is recorded in the passport, which our card mentions, so ask Customs about that.

Tourists may also buy goods in customs-zone shops within 48 hours of arrival, up to US$200 in total and up to 3 litres of spirits, where the first two litres carry 1% of the customs duty and the third 25%, with a minimum of US$13 per litre. One litre of spirits can be swapped for one carton of beer. The allowance can be claimed up to four times a year with the passport holder present, and each family member has their own.
egypt.src: Source read: Egyptian Customs Authority, Travel and tourism (in Arabic). The passport record is not mentioned on the page.

ethiopia.h: What the Ethiopian Ministry of Finance directive says about alcohol
p: Ethiopian Ministry of Finance Directive No. 923/2014 on goods imported or exported for personal use says any traveller may import for personal use, without duty or tax, 2 litres of alcoholic drink, next to 200 grams of cigarettes, 250 grams of loose tobacco and perfume allowances. The directive was circulated in 2022 and applies to travellers by land or at international airports.

The file we read is held on an airline's site, not the customs commission's, which is why the card is marked unofficial. It does not give a minimum age or a penalty for alcohol above the allowance, so check the current rules with the Ethiopian Customs Commission.
ethiopia.src: Source read: Ethiopian Ministry of Finance Directive No. 923/2014 (English copy on ethiopianairlines.com). It is an unofficial copy and states no alcohol penalty.

fiji.h: What Fiji Revenue and Customs says about the alcohol allowance
p: The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service says travellers aged 18 or over may bring up to 3 litres of spirits, 4.5 litres of wine or 4.5 litres of beer, or a mix within the same total. The goods must be carried by the traveller and not be for sale or for someone else. The tobacco allowance sits next to it: 200 cigarettes, or 200 g of cigars or tobacco, and chewing tobacco is prohibited.

Personal goods valued at FJ$2,000 or less are duty-free if for your own use, and goods over the allowance or for commercial use are subject to duty. The page does not list alcohol as a separate trigger for ticking Yes on the arrival card, which asks about prohibited or restricted items, FJ$10,000 or more in currency or biosecurity risk goods. It gives no penalty for alcohol over the allowance.
fiji.src: Source read: FRCS, Arriving in Fiji. No alcohol penalty is stated.

georgia.h: What the Georgian Revenue Service brochure says about alcohol
p: The Georgian Revenue Service customs brochure allows, per 30 calendar days, in hand luggage or baggage for personal or family use or as a gift, one of: 1 litre of alcoholic drinks of 22% alcohol or more, or 2 litres of drinks below 22%, or a combination of those two where the shares of each limit add up to no more than 100%, or 4 litres of wine and 16 litres of beer. Tax benefits for tobacco and alcohol start at age 18.

Through air checkpoints the allowance applies per calendar day instead of per 30 days. Goods up to GEL 500 and 30 kg may be imported duty-free per 30 days by road, and up to GEL 3,000 through air checkpoints. The brochure does not describe penalties for exceeding the alcohol allowance.
georgia.src: Source read: Revenue Service of Georgia, brochure on exemption of goods from duties and declaring. It states no alcohol penalty.

hong-kong.h: What Hong Kong Customs says about the liquor concession
p: Hong Kong Customs and Excise says travellers aged 18 or over may bring 1 litre of liquor with an alcohol content above 30% by volume, measured at 20 degrees Celsius, duty-free, and holders of a Hong Kong ID card must have been outside Hong Kong for at least 24 hours to use it. Hong Kong charges excise duty only on liquor, tobacco, hydrocarbon oil and methyl alcohol, and the tobacco concession is only 19 cigarettes.

Failing to declare dutiable goods above the allowance, or making a false or incomplete declaration, can lead to prosecution, or the department may impose a penalty for compoundable offences under Cap. 109. There is no concession for goods for trade or business, and cross-boundary drivers under the Northbound and Southbound schemes are not eligible.
hong-kong.src: Source read: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department, Duty-free concessions for passengers. The penalty amounts are not on the page.

iceland.h: What Icelandic Customs says about alcohol and ages
p: Icelandic Customs (Skatturinn) counts the alcohol allowance in units. It names spirits as drinks above 21% alcohol and wine as any non-beer drink at 21% or below, and gives example combinations such as 1 litre of spirits plus 0.75 litre of wine plus 3 litres of beer, or 3 litres of wine and 6 litres of beer, or 1 litre of spirits and 6 litres of beer, or 1.5 litres of wine and 12 litres of beer, or 18 litres of beer.

The minimum age for bringing alcohol into Iceland is 20 and for tobacco 18. The goods must be for personal use or gifts, not for sale, and travel agencies, guides or drivers cannot import duty-free goods on a traveller's behalf. Use the red channel if you have dutiable or restricted goods. The page does not state a penalty for exceeding the alcohol allowance.
iceland.src: Source read: Skatturinn, Duty-free imports (English). No alcohol penalty is stated.

india.h: What the Indian customs passenger guide says about alcohol
p: The Indian customs passenger guide allows alcoholic liquor, wine or beer up to 2 litres within the duty-free allowance for incoming passengers, next to 100 cigarettes, 25 cigars or 125 g of tobacco. Above the allowance, the guide gives the rate for all alcoholic beverages other than beer, including wine, as basic customs duty of 50% plus an agriculture infrastructure and development cess of 100%, and for beer basic duty of 100% plus a 10% social welfare surcharge.

These rates come from a guide that may be out of date, so check the current rates with Indian customs before you carry more than the allowance. The guide gives no minimum age and no penalty for alcohol. Some Indian states also restrict alcohol themselves, which the guide does not cover.
india.src: Source read: CBIC, Customs clearance of passengers at a glance (PDF). The rates may have changed since the guide was issued.

jamaica.h: What the Jamaica Customs Agency says about alcohol
p: The Jamaica Customs Agency page on duty-free allowances says travellers aged 18 and over may bring 2 litres of alcoholic drinks, along with 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars or 230 grams of processed tobacco, 170 ml of perfume and 340 ml of eau de toilette. Items must be properly declared, and each allowance applies only up to the stated amount.

Personal and household effects, including gifts, are exempt up to US$1,000 or the equivalent in Jamaican dollars. The page does not describe penalties for going over the alcohol allowance or the age rule for travellers under 18, so ask Customs before you travel with more.
jamaica.src: Source read: Jamaica Customs Agency, What are my duty-free allowances and exemptions. No alcohol penalty is stated.

japan.h: What Japan Customs says about the alcohol allowance and age
p: Japan Customs lists the duty-free allowance per person over 20 as 3 bottles of alcohol of about 760 ml each, next to 200 cigarettes or 50 cigars or 250 g of other tobacco. The page applies the allowances only to people over 20 and says nothing about younger travellers. Other items are allowed in any quantity as long as each item's overseas market value is 10,000 yen or less, up to 200,000 yen in total.

An item worth more than 200,000 yen gets no allowance and is taxed in full, and customs applies the allowance to the items that benefit the traveller most. The page does not state the duty rates or the procedure for alcohol above the allowance.
japan.src: Source read: Japan Customs, Customs Answer 7104 (English). Duty rates above the allowance are not on the page.

kenya.h: What the Kenya Revenue Authority says about alcohol
p: The Kenya Revenue Authority says travellers may bring up to 1 litre of spirits or liquor and up to 2 litres of wine without declaring, and perfume up to half a litre in total, with no more than a quarter of that as perfume. Duty-free purchases above these amounts must be declared. Cigarettes, cigars and tobacco are allowed up to 250 grams combined.

Passengers get a US$2,000 concession for personal or household goods, but alcohol, perfume and tobacco are not covered by it beyond the limits above. Goods bought abroad above US$500 must be declared. Failing to declare or misdeclaring goods breaches Section 203 of the East African Community Customs Management Act and goods are liable to seizure or confiscation.
kenya.src: Source read: KRA, Passenger terminal clearance in Kenya.

indonesia.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Indonesia
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Indonesia lists a duty-free allowance of 1 litre of alcohol. It states no age limit.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
indonesia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Indonesia (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

israel.h: What the Israel Tax Authority says about alcohol
p: The Israel Tax Authority says that when you enter Israel through an airport or a land border crossing after a stay of at least 3 days abroad, you may bring 1 litre of alcohol and 2 litres of wine tax-free, together with 250 ml of perfume and goods worth up to 200 US dollars. Anything above these amounts is taxed, and the rule is written for Israeli residents returning from abroad, not for tourists.
The Travel Doc customs page (unofficial) adds that the traveller must be 18 or over; the Tax Authority page does not state an age, so confirm it with customs if you are younger.
israel.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Israel Tax Authority, "Information for Israeli residents wishing to import goods in personal import" (gov.il, English, published 22 October 2025). The Travel Doc page (unofficial, read 16 November 2026) gives the age.
link: Israel Tax Authority: personal import, entering by airport or land border

jordan.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Jordan
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Jordan allows travellers aged 18 and over 1 bottle of alcohol, with a maximum capacity of 1 litre.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
jordan.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Jordan (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

norway.h: What Norwegian Customs says about alcohol quotas
p: Norwegian Customs gives the same alcohol quota to residents and visitors: 1 litre of spirits over 22% up to 60%, 1.5 litres of wine over 2.5% up to 22%, which is two bottles, and 2 litres of beer over 2.5%, or alcopops and cider up to 4.7%, which is six 0.33-litre bottles. Drinks over 60% alcohol are prohibited. You must be 18 or older to bring beer and wine and 20 or older to bring drinks above 22%.

Quotas are per person and can be combined with tobacco quotas, but tobacco cannot be swapped for alcohol. One litre of spirits can be exchanged for 1.5 litres of wine or beer, and wine can be exchanged for equal amounts of beer, but wine and beer cannot be exchanged for stronger drinks. On a stay under 24 hours you may bring alcohol once if you can document local taxes paid in an EEA country, and tax-free purchases are not allowed. You may bring more than the quota if you declare the excess. The page describes no penalties.
norway.src: Source read: Toll.no, Alcohol and tobacco quotas (English). No penalty is stated on the page.

oman.h: What Oman Customs says about alcohol for non-Muslims
p: Oman's General Directorate of Customs says non-Muslims may bring up to 2 litres of wine and 48 cans of beer, and the page states that Muslims are not allowed this exemption. The exemptions do not apply to someone, in the page's words, of the kind frequently passing the customs territory. The page mentions no minimum age.

The same page exempts up to 400 cigarettes, gifts up to a total value of 300 riyals, and electronics and household appliances in non-commercial quantities. Cash and valuables above 6,000 riyals must be declared. It lists no penalties for exceeding the alcohol exemption, so ask Omani Customs before you travel.
oman.src: Source read: Oman Customs, Traveller services. No alcohol penalty is stated.

peru.h: What SUNAT says about liquor in baggage
p: The Peruvian customs authority SUNAT says passengers over 18 may bring as exempt baggage up to 3 litres of liquor, with 20 packs of cigarettes, 50 cigars or 250 grams of loose tobacco. Personal-use goods and gifts are exempt if their combined value is up to US$500, and electrical devices, tools and professional equipment in that group are limited to one unit per type.
The page does not give a penalty for liquor above the exemption or say what happens to the excess. Check SUNAT before you travel with more than 3 litres.
peru.src: Source read: SUNAT, Equipaje y bienes (viajeros) (in Spanish). No alcohol penalty is stated.

mexico.h: What the Mexican customs agency says about alcohol
p: The Mexican customs agency (ANAM) says passengers over 18 may bring up to 3 litres of alcoholic drinks and 6 litres of wine duty-free in their personal luggage, next to 20 packs of cigarettes, 25 cigars or 200 g of tobacco. The separate US$500 goods exemption, for goods beyond personal luggage supported by an invoice or receipt, does not cover alcoholic drinks, manufactured tobacco or fuel beyond the vehicle's tank.

Family members arriving together on the same transport can combine the US$500 exemption, and customs staff may set the value if there is no receipt. The page also lists the Heroes Paisanos periods for Mexicans returning for holidays. It does not describe penalties for exceeding the alcohol allowance.
mexico.src: Source read: ANAM, Equipaje y franquicia (English). No alcohol penalty is stated.

new-zealand.h: What New Zealand Customs says about alcohol
p: New Zealand Customs says the duty-free alcohol limits are 4.5 litres of wine or beer, or 3 bottles or containers of spirits or liqueur, each holding no more than 1.125 litres. You must be 17 or older to claim the alcohol and tobacco concessions, while you must be 18 to buy these items in New Zealand. The concessions cover only personal use and gifts, not items carried for others or intended for sale.

Anything above must be declared, duty and GST are payable on the excess, and anything over your concession is charged full duties. Undeclared excess is seized and destroyed, and you may be fined or prosecuted. The NZ$700 goods concession is separate, and alcohol and tobacco have their own limits. The Customs estimator tool shows likely charges.
new-zealand.src: Source read: New Zealand Customs, Duty-free shopping.

serbia.h: What Serbian Customs says about the alcohol allowance
p: Serbian Customs allows 1 litre of spirits, or 1 litre of sparkling and liqueur wines, or a combination of the two, plus 1 litre of other wines. Beer and olive oil have no precisely defined limit, but they must clearly be for personal use and not for resale. The tobacco allowance sits next to it: 50 cigarettes, or 25 cigarillos, or 10 cigars, or 50 g of tobacco, and snus is prohibited.

The page states no minimum age for the alcohol allowance. Goods up to EUR 3,000 can be cleared at the border in the red channel with a single 10% customs rate plus VAT, usually 20%, and goods above that go through the regular procedure. Non-residents can get a VAT refund on unused goods worth at least 6,000 dinars. The page describes no penalty for alcohol above the allowance.
serbia.src: Source read: Carina.rs, FAQ for tourists (English). No age rule or penalty for alcohol is stated.

seychelles.h: What Seychelles Revenue Commission says about alcohol
p: The Seychelles Revenue Commission says passengers aged 18 and over may bring up to 2 litres of drinks at or below 16% alcohol, such as beer, wine and sparkling wine, and up to 2 litres of drinks above 16%, such as whisky, rum, gin and distilled liqueurs, plus 250 g of tobacco products or 200 cigarettes. Other goods are allowed up to SCR 15,000, including one electronic item, and perfume up to 200 ml.

Duty-free goods must be for personal use only. Passengers who exceed their allowance pay the applicable taxes on arrival, and failing to declare excess goods is a serious offence that can lead to heavy fines, seizure and possible prosecution. If you are unsure, use the red channel. The page does not state the fine amounts.
seychelles.src: Source read: Seychelles Revenue Commission, Customs and Excises. Fine amounts are not on the page.

singapore.h: What Singapore Customs says about the liquor concession
p: Singapore Customs says the liquor concession needs you to be 18 or older, to have spent at least 2 days abroad, not to arrive from Malaysia, and the liquor must be for personal use. The options are 1 litre of spirits plus 1 litre of wine, or 1 litre of spirits plus 1 litre of beer, or 1 litre of wine plus 1 litre of beer, or 2 litres of wine, or 2 litres of beer. Crew have their own smaller options, and there is no concession at all for travellers arriving from Malaysia.

Liquor above the concession incurs duty and GST, and more than 10 litres needs a Customs permit. Failing to declare goods at the Red Channel may result in fines or prosecution. The S$500 GST relief for newly bought goods excludes liquor and tobacco, and tobacco has no concession at all.
singapore.src: Source read: Singapore Customs, Duty-free concession and GST relief. Fine amounts are not on the page.

south-africa.h: What SARS says about the alcohol allowance
p: The South African Revenue Service guide on duty-free allowances for travellers says a traveller may import free of duty and tax 2 litres of wine and 1 litre of other alcoholic drinks, including beer, along with 200 cigarettes, 20 cigars, 250 g of tobacco, 250 ml of eau de toilette and 50 ml of perfume. The tobacco and alcohol allowances are not available to anyone under 18, and crew members are not entitled to any duty-free consumables.

Consumables above the limits cannot be claimed under the duty-free allowance, and full duty and VAT must be paid on the excess. The allowance may be used once per person in a 30-day cycle after an absence of more than 48 hours. A flat rate allowance lets you bring additional goods up to R20,000 at 20%. The guide does not describe penalties for undeclared alcohol.
south-africa.src: Source read: SARS, SC-PA-01-03 Duty-free allowances for travellers (external guide, PDF). Penalties are not in the part read.

south-korea.h: What Korea Customs says about the liquor allowance
p: The Korea Customs Service page on duty-free allowances says liquor has its own allowance of up to 2 litres together with US$400, which applies outside the US$800 general limit, with 200 cigarette sticks for tobacco and 100 ml of perfume. The page does not list a limit of 1 litre. Minors under 19, counted by year of birth, are not given the tax exemption for liquor and cigarettes.

If you declare goods above the allowances yourself, you get a 30% reduction from the standard customs duty. Undeclared goods found later face an additional tax of 40% above the regular tax, or 60% if caught two or more times within 2 years.
south-korea.src: Source read: Korea Customs Service, duty-free allowance page (English).

sri-lanka.h: What Sri Lanka Customs says about the alcohol allowance
p: Sri Lanka Customs says Sri Lankan residents may bring in 2.5 litres of liquor and foreigners 1.5 litres. The liquor must be bought at Sri Lanka Duty Free shops or brought from abroad on the day of arrival, and liquor sent as unaccompanied baggage is not duty-free. Our card gives the tourist allowance as two regular bottles, so the page's 1.5 litres is the figure to plan on.

The page also says cigarettes, cigars, beedies and snuff are not allowed as personal baggage at all. The general allowances apply only to Sri Lankan passport holders, residence visa holders and qualifying dual citizens, based on time abroad. The page describes no penalty for alcohol above the allowance.
sri-lanka.src: Source read: Sri Lanka Customs, Passenger Services Directorate. No alcohol penalty is stated.

kuwait.h: What the UK government advice says about alcohol in Kuwait
p: We re-read the UK government's travel advice for Kuwait. It lists alcohol among the goods that are illegal to import, together with narcotics, gambling machines, pork and pork products and pornographic material. It gives no specific penalty for alcohol.

The page gives general penalties for failing to declare goods that may be prohibited or taxable: imprisonment, refusal of entry and possible deportation, but it ties them to non-declaration, not explicitly to alcohol. This is the advice of another country's government, which is why the card is marked unofficial. Check Kuwaiti customs before you travel.
kuwait.src: Source read: UK government (FCDO), Kuwait entry requirements. This is an unofficial source and states no alcohol penalty.

slovakia.h: What the Slovak Financial Administration says about alcohol in luggage
p: The Slovak Financial Administration says travellers aged 17 or over may carry alcohol in their luggage, for non-commercial and occasional use: up to 1 litre of spirits over 22% or 2 litres of spirits at 22% or below, 2 litres of sparkling wine and similar drinks, 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. Each allowance counts as 100%, and mixed products are allowed if the shares add up to no more than 100%.

The value limits for the VAT and customs exemption in luggage are EUR 430 by air, EUR 300 by other transport and EUR 150 for anyone under 15. Excess quantities are taxed in Slovakia, and spirit consumer packs without a Slovak control stamp cannot be released for free circulation. The page describes no penalties.
slovakia.src: Source read: Finančná správa, Oslobodenie od cla, DPH a SPD (in Slovak). No penalties are stated.

nepal.h: What the Nepal aeronautical information publication says about alcohol
p: The passenger customs section of the Nepal aeronautical information publication says no customs duty is levied on goods brought by a foreign passenger holding a passport up to one bottle of liquor of up to one litre or up to twelve cans of beer, together with 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars and 250 grams of tobacco, medicines up to NPR 10,000, foodstuffs up to NPR 5,000 and fresh fruit up to NPR 2,000.

The publication is an aviation document of the Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal, not a page of the Customs Department, so it does not give an age limit or a penalty. It reads as one bottle or twelve cans, so we cannot say whether a bottle and cans can be combined; ask Nepal Customs.
nepal.src: Source read: Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal, AIP Nepal, customs section. It gives no age limit or penalty.

taiwan.h: What Taipei Customs says about alcohol
p: Taipei Customs says passengers aged 18 or over may bring 1.5 litres of alcohol duty-free, with an overall limit of 5 litres including the duty-free amount, and alcohol declared as of Chinese origin is limited to 1 litre in total. Alcohol means drinks above 0.5% alcohol by volume plus other ethyl products for manufacturing. Our card says 1.5 litres, and the page does not mention a 1-litre duty-free figure for other alcohol.

For tobacco and alcohol above the allowance the page gives fines and confiscation, for example NTD 1,000 per 200 cigarettes, and dutiable goods may be confiscated or fined up to three times their value. E-cigarettes and e-liquids are prohibited, and carrying prohibited goods may lead to criminal penalties. Tobacco and alcohol are excluded from the NTD 35,000 personal goods limit.
taiwan.src: Source read: Customs Administration, Taipei Customs, duty-free page (English). Rates may have changed, so check the current amounts.

thailand.h: What Thai Customs says about the alcohol allowance
p: The Suvarnabhumi Airport customs page for the Nothing to Declare channel allows up to 1 litre of alcohol, together with 200 cigarettes or 250 g of tobacco and personal belongings worth up to 20,000 baht, excluding prohibited or restricted goods and food. Any excess cigarettes, tobacco or alcohol must be put in the box provided by Customs, and the page warns that otherwise prosecution will be carried out.

In the Red Channel you bring your passport and any invoices or receipts, and non-commercial accompanying belongings up to 200,000 baht are assessed a flat rate of duty and taxes. Prohibited or restricted goods lead to prosecution. The page gives no minimum age for the alcohol allowance.
thailand.src: Source read: Thai Customs Department, Suvarnabhumi Airport green channel page. The age rule is not on it.

turkey.h: What the Turkish customs guide says about the alcohol allowance
p: The Turkish customs guide says a traveller may bring up to 1 litre of spirits above 22% alcohol or up to 2 litres of drinks at or below 22%, next to 600 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars, 250 g of cut tobacco and 250 g of pipe tobacco. Each product has its own quantity limit, and the allowance cannot be exceeded for any single product. Travellers under 18 cannot claim the tobacco or alcohol allowances, and the items must be with the traveller.

The page states no monetary value limit for these allowances, and a related question on its index mentions 1,500 euros for a single item without explaining it. It does not give a penalty for going over, so check Turkish Customs for the current rules.
turkey.src: Source read: Gümrük Rehberi (Turkish customs guide), traveller allowances (in Turkish). No penalty is stated.

united-arab-emirates.h: What the UAE government portal says about the alcohol allowance
p: The official UAE government portal says a traveller may bring up to 4 litres of alcoholic drinks or 2 cartons of beer of 24 cans each, with no can above 355 ml, along with 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars or 500 g of tobacco. Gifts, perfumes and personal luggage together must not exceed AED 3,000, must be limited in quantity and not commercial, and the traveller must not be a frequent carrier of goods or crew.

Customs duty plus VAT applies above these limits, and the page states no rate. It sets no minimum age for alcohol, so check the age rule with UAE customs and the rules of the emirate where you land, because alcohol rules differ between emirates. Our card says to respect the local law, which the page does not discuss.
united-arab-emirates.src: Source read: u.ae, Customs clearance. The duty rate on the excess and the age rule are not on the page.

united-kingdom.h: What GOV.UK says about the alcohol allowance for Great Britain
p: GOV.UK gives the alcohol allowance for Great Britain as 42 litres of beer and cider, 18 litres of still or sparkling wine, 4 litres of spirits and other products over 22% alcohol by volume, and 9 litres of products up to 22%, excluding beer, cider and wine, such as fortified wine. If you go over an allowance, you pay tax and duty on all of that product, and your goods could be seized if you do not declare them. You declare online before travelling or at the border.

For travellers aged 17 or under there are no personal allowances for alcohol, tobacco or vaping products; you can bring them for your own use but must declare them before arriving. Other goods are allowed up to GBP 390, or GBP 270 by private plane or boat, and above that you pay tax and duty on the whole value. The page covers Great Britain only, and Northern Ireland has its own guide.
united-kingdom.src: Source read: GOV.UK, Duty-free goods: arriving in Great Britain.

united-states.h: What U.S. Customs and Border Protection says about alcohol
p: U.S. Customs and Border Protection says one American litre, 33.8 fluid ounces, of alcohol can count toward a returning resident's personal exemption if it is for your own use, not for resale, and legal in the state where you arrive. You must be at least 21, states may set stricter limits and CBP enforces them, and alcohol beyond the duty-free amount is taxed even if your total exemption is not used up.

The standard exemption is US$800, and items above it but within the flat-rate limit are dutiable at a flat 3%. The tobacco exemption covers not more than 200 cigarettes and 100 cigars, and amounts beyond that can be detained, seized or penalised. The page does not mention a US$100 gift allowance.
united-states.src: Source read: CBP, Customs duty information for international visitors.

vietnam.h: What Vietnam Law Magazine says about the alcohol allowance
p: Vietnam Law Magazine, an English-language legal publication, reports in an article dated 16 September 2026 that under Decree 273/2026/ND-CP, Article 5, the 1.5-litre alcohol allowance covers drinks with 20% or more alcohol, below 20% the limit is 2 litres, and other spirits and beer are capped at 3 litres. An unopened container may still be duty-exempt if the excess is no more than 1 litre, and anything beyond 1 litre is dutiable.

The alcohol and tobacco allowances do not apply to anyone under 18, and other goods can be duty-exempt if their total customs value is no more than VND 10 million. The article gives no effective date for the decree and no penalties. It is a magazine, not a Vietnamese authority, which is why the card is marked unofficial.
vietnam.src: Source read: Vietnam Law Magazine, article of 16 September 2026. This is an unofficial source.

switzerland.h: What the Swiss customs office says about alcohol allowances
p: The Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Security says duty-free allowances for food, alcohol and tobacco apply per person per day, and that if the total value of goods you bring exceeds CHF 150, VAT is payable in any case. Foodstuffs ordered abroad and delivered by post or courier follow different rules.

The table of quantities, including the alcohol figures our card gives, did not appear in the text we could read, so we cannot re-confirm the 5 litres figure or the age rule here. For the exact quantities and any penalties, the page points to the customs information office on +41 58 467 15 15. Check the table on the Swiss customs page before you travel.
switzerland.src: Source read: FOCBS (BAZG), Duty-free allowances: foodstuffs, alcohol and tobacco. The quantities table was not in the text read.

malaysia.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Malaysia
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Malaysia lists a duty-free allowance of 1 litre of alcohol, for non-residents staying more than 72 hours and for Malaysian residents who have been abroad for more than 72 hours.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
malaysia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Malaysia (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

maldives.h: Alcohol in Maldives: the card, an unofficial source and the general rule
p: Our card says that importing alcohol without prior approval is prohibited under Maldivian law and that alcohol is confiscated on arrival. It comes from the prohibited and restricted items page of Maldives Customs that we link below the card.

We could not re-open the official page, so we checked the UK government's travel advice for Maldives, an unofficial source. On alcohol it says that alcohol is illegal to bring in, as contrary to Islam, together with pork products. Most countries cap duty-free alcohol by volume and by age, and charge duty or confiscate the excess. We could not confirm more for Maldives than the card says, so ask Maldives Customs if you plan to carry more.
maldives.src: UK government (FCDO) entry requirements page, read 16 November 2026. It is an unofficial source: it is another country's travel advice.

mauritius.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Mauritius
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Mauritius allows travellers aged 18 and over one of: 1 litre of spirits plus 2 litres of wine and beer, or 2 litres of spirits, or 4 litres of wine and beer.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
mauritius.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Mauritius (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

morocco.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Morocco
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Morocco lists 1 litre of spirits and 1 litre of wine as free to import. It states no age limit.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
morocco.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Morocco (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

nigeria.h: Alcohol in Nigeria: the card, an unofficial source and the general rule
p: Our card says the passenger concessions list one 1-litre bottle of spirit and one of wine, so one bottle each. It comes from the passenger concessions page of the Nigeria Customs Service that we link below the card.

We could not re-open the official page, so we checked the UK government's travel advice for Nigeria, an unofficial source. On alcohol it says that importing beer and sparkling wine is illegal. A small allowance per adult is the norm, with a higher age limit than for tobacco in many places, and drinks above the allowance are taxed or taken. the Nigeria Customs Service sets the allowance for Nigeria, and the card shows the figure we have.
nigeria.src: UK government (FCDO) entry requirements page, read 16 November 2026. It is an unofficial source: it is another country's travel advice.

philippines.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in the Philippines
p: The Travel Doc customs page for the Philippines allows travellers aged 18 and over 2 bottles of alcohol with a total value of 10,000 pesos or less.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
philippines.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for the Philippines (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.
link: Travel Doc: the Philippines customs information

russia.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Russia
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Russia allows travellers aged 18 and over up to 5 litres of alcohol.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
russia.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Russia (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

ukraine.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about alcohol in Ukraine
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Ukraine allows travellers aged 18 and over 1 litre of spirits and 2 litres of wine.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
ukraine.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Ukraine (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

qatar.h: What Qatar’s customs authority says about alcohol
p: Qatar’s General Authority of Customs page for individuals importing goods lists alcoholic drinks among the goods whose import is restricted under the GCC Common Customs Law. It says such goods need prior permission from the competent authorities before they are imported.

The page speaks about individuals who import an item personally or buy it online; it does not state a personal allowance for travellers arriving at the airport, and it shows no update date (the footer reads 2020). We therefore give no litre figure: confirm with Qatar customs or your airline before you pack alcohol for Qatar.
qatar.src: Source read 16 November 2026: General Authority of Customs, Qatar (customs.gov.qa), Importing goods under a personal name (undated).
link: Qatar General Authority of Customs: importing goods under a personal name

saudi-arabia.h: Alcohol in Saudi Arabia: the card, an unofficial source and the general rule
p: Our card says Saudi Arabia bans the import of alcohol and intoxicants of all kinds, with penalties, according to the ZATCA prohibited goods page that we link below the card.

We could not re-open the official page, so we checked the UK government's travel advice for Saudi Arabia, an unofficial source. On alcohol it says that importing alcohol is illegal. Airport duty-free shops sell within the same allowance, so what you buy on the way counts. For Saudi Arabia, check ZATCA, the Saudi customs authority if you are close to the card figure.
saudi-arabia.src: UK government (FCDO) entry requirements page, read 16 November 2026. It is an unofficial source: it is another country's travel advice.

finland.h: What the Finnish Customs leaflet says about alcohol
p: Finnish Customs’ leaflet for travellers (6/2021) sets the tax-free allowance for alcohol from outside the EU at 16 litres of beer and 4 litres of still wine, plus either 1 litre of spirits (over 22% and up to 80%) or 2 litres of other drinks of 22% or less. Strong and mild drinks can be combined proportionally; this does not apply to still wine or beer.

Persons under 18 may not bring alcohol into Finland, and persons under 20 only mild drinks. Spirits above 80% need a permit. Arriving from outside the EEA by means other than air, a visitor living outside the EEA may bring alcohol only if staying in Finland over 72 hours. The leaflet is from 2021, so check tulli.fi for current figures.
finland.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Finnish Customs leaflet "Customs advice for travellers" (6/2021), read as a copy hosted by expat-finland.com. The tulli.fi pages could not be opened. The leaflet is from 2021 and says to check tulli.fi for current rules.
link: Finnish Customs: Customs advice for travellers (6/2021 leaflet, hosted copy)

france.h: What French Customs adds on alcohol
p: The French customs page for goods brought back from outside the EU gives 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus either 1 litre of drinks above 22% or 2 litres of drinks of 22% or less. It says the allowances can be combined proportionally within one category of goods.

People under 17 cannot import tobacco or alcohol duty-free. The separate value allowance is 430 euros for travellers of 15 or over arriving by air or sea, and the value of goods under quantity limits is not counted in it. The page shows no update date; it refers to a customs circular of 28 April 2023.
france.src: Source read 16 November 2026: French Customs (douane.gouv.fr), page on tobacco, alcohol and other goods bought outside the EU (undated).
link: French Customs: goods bought outside the EU

greece.h: What the Greek customs authority (AADE) says about alcohol
p: AADE allows travellers arriving from outside the EU 1 litre of spirits above 22% vol (or undenatured ethyl alcohol of 80% vol or more), or 2 litres of alcohol and drinks up to 22% vol, or a proportional mix, plus 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. Travellers under 17 get no allowance for alcohol or tobacco; this is the official age, not the 18 given by some travel sites.

The goods allowance for everything else is 430 euros for air and sea passengers and 300 euros for other travellers, 150 euros for travellers under 15 by any transport. Personal luggage that is re-exported and medicines for your own needs do not count towards it. Questions go to AADE on 1521 (free, working days 7:00 to 20:00).
greece.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Greek Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE), "Frequently asked questions - answers on exemptions for travellers from third countries", version 2.0 of 3 April 2026 (aade.gr, in Greek, translated by us).
link: AADE: Tax relief for third-country travellers (FAQ PDF, Greek)

hungary.h: Alcohol in Hungary: the card, an unofficial source and the general rule
p: Our card gives the EU rule that applies in Hungary: arriving from outside the EU you may bring 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus 1 litre of spirits over 22% or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine.

We could not re-open the official page, so we checked the UK government's travel advice for Hungary, an unofficial source. On alcohol it says that strict rules apply to alcohol and tobacco but gives no amounts. Alcohol is usually counted in litres by type, spirits, wine and beer, and a traveller who mixes types is held to the combined share. In Hungary, the Hungarian tax and customs authority (NAV) decides how that works, and the card shows the quantities.
hungary.src: UK government (FCDO) entry requirements page, read 16 November 2026. It is an unofficial source: it is another country's travel advice.

lithuania.h: What Lithuanian Customs says about alcohol
p: Lithuanian Customs says one person over 17 arriving from outside the EU by any transport may bring 1 litre of spirits above 22% vol or 2 litres of liqueur, sparkling wine, vermouth or cider up to 22%, plus 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer. Crew and border-zone residents get only 0.5 litre of strong spirits or 0.75 litre of weaker drinks, plus 0.75 litre of still wine and 4 litres of beer. Spirits from Russia and Belarus are banned from import.

From another EU country, Hinterland Travel (unofficial) lists own-use amounts that customs does not treat as trade: 10 litres of spirits, 20 litres of other drinks under 22%, 90 litres of wine (60 of it sparkling) and 110 litres of beer, with excise already paid there.
lithuania.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Lithuanian Customs (Lietuvos Respublikos muitine), "Coming from third countries" (muitine.lrv.lt, English; read from an archived copy because the live site refuses our reader). EU-travel figures from Hinterland Travel (unofficial, read 23 November 2026).
link: Lithuanian Customs: coming from third countries

malta.h: What the Maltese tax and customs administration says about alcohol
p: From a non-EU country, travellers aged 17 or over may bring, free of duty and VAT: in total 1 litre of drinks above 22% alcohol (or undenatured ethyl alcohol of 80% and over), or 2 litres of drinks at 22% or below, or a mix in proportion (for example half a litre of the stronger and one litre of the weaker). On top of that come 16 litres of beer and 4 litres of still wine.
