sweden.h: What Swedish Customs (Tullverket) says about travelling with cash
p: Tullverket says you must notify Swedish Customs if you carry cash or equivalent assets worth EUR 10,000 or more when you travel to or from Sweden, and there is no upper limit on how much you may carry. Besides notes and coins, it counts traveller's cheques, cheques, promissory notes, investment gold of at least 99.5% and gold coins of at least 90%. From 1 April 2026 the duty also applies to travel to or from other EU countries, not only non-EU countries.

You report through the online service, and if you do you need not contact customs at the border but should be able to show your registration number if asked, or you hand a paper cash declaration form to a customs officer at the border. Reporting costs nothing and has no age limit. Carrying investment gold worth more than EUR 10,000 also needs a declaration. The page does not describe penalties or say whether customs can hold the cash.
sweden.src: Source read: Tullverket, Travelling with cash and/or equivalent assets (English). Penalties are not on the page.

switzerland.h: What the Swiss Federal Office for Customs says about cash
p: The Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) says you may carry unlimited cash, foreign currency and bearer instruments such as shares, bonds and cheques into, through or out of Switzerland without declaring them. If you carry CHF 10,000 or more, or customs suspects you do, you will be asked who you are, where the money comes from, what it is for and who owns it, and the amount is recorded in the office's information system.

You must answer truthfully when questioned. Refusing to answer or giving false information is a customs offence that can bring a penalty, and if money laundering or terrorist financing is suspected, the cash may be seized temporarily and handed to the police. The same applies to cash you take out. The page does not discuss EU or Schengen rules and points to other countries' authorities for their rules.
switzerland.src: Source read: FOCBS (BAZG), Cash, foreign currency, securities (English). It does not state the size of the penalty.

taiwan.h: What a Taiwan Customs office says about currency limits
p: A Kaohsiung Customs FAQ page says each passenger may carry up to NT$100,000 and up to RMB 20,000 into or out of Taiwan. Amounts above those limits must be declared or are liable to confiscation, and even with a declaration, the excess cannot be brought in or out.

For other foreign currencies, amounts above US$10,000 or the equivalent must be declared, and once you have declared, there is no limit on the amount. The same goes for traveller's cheques, other cheques, promissory notes, bills of exchange and similar instruments with a total face value above US$10,000. The page does not mention gold. It says that if the English and Chinese versions differ, the Chinese one prevails. This is a regional office page, so check the Customs Administration for the current limits.
taiwan.src: Source read: Customs Administration, Kaohsiung Customs, FAQ page (English). Gold and the exact penalty are not on the page.

thailand.h: What the Bank of Thailand says about carrying banknotes
p: The Bank of Thailand exchange control page says foreign currency and Thai baht banknotes can be brought into Thailand with no limit on the amount. Bringing in or taking out more than THB 450,000 in baht banknotes, or more than US$15,000 or the equivalent in foreign banknotes, needs a customs declaration when you enter or leave.

Taking money out has its own limits. Foreign banknotes may leave only up to the amount you bought from an authorised bank or money changer. Baht banknotes may leave up to THB 2 million for neighbouring countries (Vietnam and China's Yunnan province among them, plus the countries bordering Thailand) and up to THB 50,000 for other countries. The page lists no penalties. Our card also notes that Thai Customs' own English page still shows an older US$20,000 threshold, so declare anything above US$15,000 to be safe.
thailand.src: Source read: Bank of Thailand, Exchange control regulation. Penalties are not on the page.

turkey.h: What the Turkish Ministry of Trade says about taking cash out
p: The Turkish Ministry of Trade customs FAQ says a traveller taking out more than TL 25,000 or more than EUR 10,000, or the equivalent, must declare it to a customs officer. The two amounts cannot be combined, and amounts below the limit need no declaration. The declaration is made in writing on the Nakit Beyan Formu (Cash Declaration Form), which you request at border customs. Cash found in a search without a written declaration counts as undeclared.

Declared cash of EUR 10,000 or more carries no fine, fee or tax. Failing to declare, or giving false or misleading information, brings an administrative fine of 10% of the undeclared amount, the cash is held, and the case is reported to the Chief Public Prosecutor's Office and the Financial Crimes Investigation Board (MASAK). Cash in certain categories, such as personal debts, gifts, inheritance or dividends, may leave Turkey only through banks and is seized if carried by a traveller. The page is about leaving Turkey. One answer on it gives 9,999 euros as the threshold for some routes, so declare at EUR 10,000 to be safe.
turkey.src: Source read: T.C. Ticaret Bakanlığı, Gümrük Muhafaza FAQ (in Turkish). The page covers taking cash out of Turkey.

united-arab-emirates.h: What the UAE government portal says about declaring cash
p: The official UAE government portal says passengers entering or leaving the UAE with more than AED 60,000 in cash must declare it to the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Ports Security (ICP). The threshold also covers the equivalent in other currencies, financial instruments, precious metals and valuable stones. For passengers under 18, the amount they carry is added to the limit of the parent, guardian or person accompanying them.

You declare online at the ICP customs website (declare.customs.ae) or in the Afseh app, and Abu Dhabi also lists a separate cash disclosure e-service on TAMM. The page does not mention penalties for failing to declare.
united-arab-emirates.src: Source read: u.ae, Customs clearance. Penalties are not on the page.

united-kingdom.h: What GOV.UK says about bringing cash into and out of the UK
p: GOV.UK says you must declare cash of GBP 10,000 or more when you carry it between Great Britain and a country outside the UK. In Northern Ireland the threshold is EUR 10,000, and the rules differ there: carrying EUR 10,000 or more between Northern Ireland and a non-EU country needs a declaration, so does arriving in Northern Ireland from Great Britain with that amount, but travelling from Northern Ireland to Great Britain does not. Family or group totals count even if each person carries less.

Cash means notes and coins, bearer bonds, traveller's cheques and signed cheques not made out to a named person or organisation; in Northern Ireland it also covers money orders, gold and prepaid cards. You declare before you leave the UK, or on arrival or before travel, and the earliest is 72 hours before the trip. You do it online on GOV.UK and get a reference number, by calling the Customs and International Trade Helpline, or by telling a Border Force officer at the red channel. Undeclared cash can be seized, and getting it back may need a penalty of up to GBP 5,000. Cash can also be held for 48 hours on reasonable suspicion of crime, after which a court order is needed.
united-kingdom.src: Source read: GOV.UK, Bringing cash into or out of the UK.

united-states.h: What U.S. Customs and Border Protection says about reporting money
p: U.S. Customs and Border Protection says you must report currency or monetary instruments totalling more than US$10,000 when you enter or leave the United States, whether you are travelling for business, sending money abroad or bringing home savings. The page sets no maximum amount you may carry. For families or groups the threshold applies to the combined total, not to each person.

You file FinCEN Form 105, preferably online, or on paper handed to a CBP officer, before you leave or when you arrive, and Mobile Passport Control users can file there. Monetary instruments include U.S. and foreign coins and currency, traveller's cheques, and bearer-form or endorsed-in-blank negotiable instruments such as cheques, promissory notes and money orders. Failing to file or giving false information can lead to seizure and forfeiture of the money, and civil or criminal penalties, including fines or prison, may apply.
united-states.src: Source read: CBP, Money and monetary instruments.

vietnam.h: What Vietnam Law Magazine says about carrying cash
p: Vietnam Law Magazine, an English-language legal publication, says in an article dated 7 October 2023 that you may carry any amount through an international border gate, but cash above US$5,000 or VND 15 million, or the equivalent, must be declared on a form handed to the border-gate customs office. The thresholds apply to cash in dong, dollars or another foreign currency, and do not apply to traveller's cheques, bank cards, savings books or securities.

The article adds that people carrying less than US$5,000 in foreign currency must also file if they plan to pay it into a foreign-currency account at a licensed bank, because the customs-certified form supports the deposit. It mentions no penalties and no other procedure or charge. This is a magazine, not a Vietnamese authority, which is why the card is marked unofficial. Check Vietnamese customs before you travel.
vietnam.src: Source read: Vietnam Law Magazine, Bringing cash to Vietnam (7 October 2023). This is an unofficial source.

ukraine.h: What the Travel Doc customs page says about cash in Ukraine
p: The Travel Doc customs page for Ukraine says funds above 10,000 hryvnia need a written declaration supported by documents showing the money was withdrawn from an accredited bank or similar institution. Its wording on funds below that level is unclear, so ask Ukrainian customs which amounts you must declare.
The page names no publisher and shows no date, so confirm the figures with the customs authority before you travel.
ukraine.src: Unofficial source, read 16 November 2026: Travel Doc customs information page for Ukraine (infopages.traveldoc.aero, undated; it names no publisher). The official customs site could not be read.

european-union.h: What the EU Your Europe page says about carrying cash
p: The EU's Your Europe page says anyone entering or leaving the EU with EUR 10,000 or more in cash, or the equivalent in other currencies, must declare it, and the same goes for listed commodities of that value. You declare to the customs authorities of the EU country you enter or leave, on the EU cash declaration form. Customs can also act on smaller amounts that appear linked to crime. Cash means banknotes and coins, including discontinued currency that banks still exchange, bearer negotiable instruments such as traveller's cheques and signed cheques, promissory notes or money orders with no named payee, coins with at least 90% gold and bullion with at least 99.5% gold.

There are no EU-wide rules for carrying cash between EU countries, so you check with the customs authorities of the countries you leave, enter and pass through. For cash of EUR 10,000 or more sent by post, freight or courier, customs may require a disclosure declaration from the sender, recipient or their representative within 30 days of a request. Failing to declare, or declaring wrongly or incompletely, leads to penalties set by each country, and customs may check people, baggage and vehicles. The rules come from Regulation (EU) 2018/1672, and the form from Regulation (EU) 2021/776.
european-union.src: Source read: Your Europe, Rules for taking cash in and out of the EU (English). Penalty amounts are set by each country and are not on the page.

european-union.h: What the EU plant health page says about travellers
p: The European Commission page on trade in plants with non-EU countries says plants, plant products and other objects listed in Annexes XI and XII of Regulation (EU) 2019/2072 must have a phytosanitary certificate from the plant protection authority of the exporting country. It is prohibited to bring plants, plant products and other objects into EU territory in personal luggage unless they come with the certificate. Some goods are banned outright, and high-risk plants are provisionally banned under Regulation (EU) 2018/2019.

For passengers, plants to be planted, fruit, vegetables and cut flowers need a certificate in the luggage. Pineapple, coconut, durian, banana and date fruit do not. Once inside the EU, a plant passport can replace the certificate for certain items. The page also refers to Regulation (EU) 2019/2122 for small consignments sent to private persons and lists exemptions for trial or scientific material, goods in the frontier zone and goods in transit. Each member state applies the rules through its own authorities, so check the national page too.
european-union.src: Source read: European Commission, Trade in plants and plant products with non-EU countries.

canada.h: What the Canada Border Services Agency says about vaping products
p: The Canada Border Services Agency says non-residents and temporary residents must declare all tobacco and vaping products when they enter Canada, and the minimum age is 18 wherever you enter. For vaping products the limit is 12 vaping containers or fewer, with a maximum of 120 mL of liquid or 120 g of solid.

The page does not call vaping products within these limits duty-free. It says duties and taxes could apply to limited quantities and that you should be ready to pay them on any declared amount. Amounts above the limits may need a permit from the provincial or territorial authority, and vaping products cannot count as exempt gifts. It states no penalty for undeclared vaping products.
canada.src: Source read: CBSA, What can I bring: tobacco and vaping products for non-residents. No penalty for undeclared vaping products is stated.

fiji.h: What Fiji Revenue and Customs says about e-cigarettes
p: The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service lists e-cigarette liquid inside the tobacco allowance for travellers aged 18 or over: e-cigarettes are capped at 200 ml or 200 mg, next to 200 cigarettes or 200 g of cigars or tobacco. Chewing tobacco is prohibited. The goods must be carried by the traveller and not be for sale or for someone else.

Goods over the allowance, or intended for commercial use, are subject to duty. The page does not list tobacco or e-cigarettes as a separate trigger for ticking Yes on the arrival card, and it describes no penalty for e-cigarettes above 200 ml.
fiji.src: Source read: FRCS, Arriving in Fiji. No e-cigarette penalty is stated.

norway.h: What Norwegian Customs says about nicotine products and vapes
p: Norwegian Customs says unapproved new tobacco and nicotine products, such as nicotine pouches and heated tobacco, waterpipe tobacco and certain e-cigarettes, are not allowed to be brought in under the tobacco quota page. The quota itself is 200 cigarettes or 250 g of other tobacco for visitors from outside Norway.

The page does not name which e-cigarettes are covered, does not give a quantity for permitted ones, and describes no penalty. You may bring more than the quota only if you declare the excess, but that does not make a banned product legal. Check the Norwegian customs rules for the exact product before you pack a device or liquid.
norway.src: Source read: Toll.no, Alcohol and tobacco quotas (English). The list of banned e-cigarettes and any penalty are not on the page.

taiwan.h: What Taipei Customs says about e-cigarettes
p: Taipei Customs says e-cigarettes and e-liquids are prohibited, as are undeclared or unapproved designated tobacco products, and that carrying prohibited goods may lead to criminal penalties. Only government-approved designated tobacco products count within the 200-product duty-free allowance for passengers aged 20 or over.

For tobacco above the allowance the page gives fines and confiscation, for example NTD 1,000 per 200 cigarettes, and dutiable goods may be confiscated or fined up to three times their value. The page does not describe a specific penalty for a vape device, so treat it as an item not to pack.
taiwan.src: Source read: Customs Administration, Taipei Customs, duty-free page (English). A device-specific penalty is not stated.

serbia.h: What Serbian Customs says about vapes and nicotine pouches
p: Serbian Customs lists e-cigarettes, vapes, nicotine pouches and hookah flavours for personal use as allowed alongside the tobacco allowance of 50 cigarettes, 25 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of tobacco, and says snus is prohibited. The page gives no separate quantity for e-liquid or devices.

Goods up to EUR 3,000 can be cleared at the border in the red channel with a single 10% customs rate plus VAT, and the page states no minimum age for these products and no penalty. Because quantities are not stated, keep to amounts that are clearly for personal use.
serbia.src: Source read: Carina.rs, FAQ for tourists (English). No quantity, age rule or penalty for vapes is stated.

south-korea.h: What Korea Customs says about e-cigarette liquid
p: The Korea Customs Service page on duty-free allowances sets the tobacco allowance at 200 cigarette sticks, or e-cigarette or liquid nicotine up to 20 ml with nicotine under 1%. Minors under 19, counted by year of birth, are not given the tax exemption for liquor and cigarettes. The page does not mention cigars or loose tobacco.

If you declare goods above the allowances yourself, you get a 30% reduction from the standard customs duty. Undeclared goods found later face an additional tax of 40% above the regular tax, or 60% if caught two or more times within 2 years.
south-korea.src: Source read: Korea Customs Service, duty-free allowance page (English). The page does not say whether the 20 ml counts per device or in total.

georgia.h: What the Georgian Revenue Service brochure says about e-cigarette liquid
p: The Georgian Revenue Service customs brochure allows 50 ml of e-cigarette liquid, imported as hand luggage or baggage for personal or family use or as a gift, as one of the tobacco options: per 30 calendar days by road and per calendar day through air checkpoints. Heated tobacco products are counted as 200 pieces, and capsules with tobacco content as 10 pieces.

Combinations of tobacco products are allowed if the shares of each product, measured against its own limit, add up to no more than 100%. Tax benefits for tobacco and alcohol start at age 18. The brochure does not describe penalties for liquid above 50 ml.
georgia.src: Source read: Revenue Service of Georgia, brochure on exemption of goods from duties and declaring. It states no vape penalty.

qatar.h: What the UK government advice says about vapes in Qatar
p: We read the UK government's travel advice for Qatar. It says vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal to import and sell, including liquids and electronic shisha pipes, regardless of quantity and intended use, and that customs may confiscate them. It also says drugs are strictly controlled and that medicines should be checked with the Qatari embassy.

This is the advice of another country's government, which is why this is an unofficial source. The page gives no fine amount for vapes, but it says breaking the Qatari rules on money or goods can lead to a fine or imprisonment plus seizure.
qatar.src: Source read: UK government (FCDO), Qatar entry requirements, 16 November 2026. This is an unofficial source.

united-kingdom.h: What GOV.UK says about vaping products for Great Britain
p: GOV.UK says that for travellers aged 17 or under there are no personal allowances for alcohol, tobacco or vaping products; you can bring them for your own use but must declare them before arriving in Great Britain. Your goods could be seized if you do not declare them, and you declare online before travelling or at the border.

The page does not give a quantity limit for vaping products for adults, and the page covers Great Britain only, so check the separate guide for Northern Ireland. The tobacco allowance on the same page is one of 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars, 250 g of tobacco or 200 sticks for heated tobacco devices.
united-kingdom.src: Source read: GOV.UK, Duty-free goods: arriving in Great Britain. No adult quantity limit for vapes is stated.

thailand.h: What the Thai customs green channel page says about e-cigarettes
p: The Suvarnabhumi Airport customs page for the Nothing to Declare channel lists the allowance as up to 200 cigarettes, or 250 g of tobacco, or 250 g of all types combined, plus 1 litre of alcohol. It does not mention e-cigarettes or whether they are prohibited, so the page gives no basis to carry a vape.

Excess cigarettes, tobacco or alcohol must be put in the box provided by Customs, and the page warns that otherwise prosecution will be carried out. Prohibited or restricted goods lead to prosecution. Because Thailand treats vapes under its own rules, which this page does not cover, ask Thai Customs before you pack a device.
thailand.src: Source read: Thai Customs Department, Suvarnabhumi Airport green channel page. E-cigarettes are not covered on it.

japan.h: What Japan Customs says about tobacco and heated tobacco
p: Japan Customs lists the duty-free tobacco allowance per person over 20 as 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 10 packages of heat-not-burn tobacco, or 250 g of other tobacco products. The page applies the allowances only to people over 20 and says nothing about younger travellers, and it does not mention nicotine e-liquid.

An item worth more than 200,000 yen gets no allowance and is taxed in full. The page does not state the duty rates or the procedure for quantities above the allowance, so a nicotine vape device or liquid is not covered by what we read and should be checked with Japan Customs.
japan.src: Source read: Japan Customs, Customs Answer 7104 (English). Nicotine liquid is not covered on the page.

brazil.h: What Anvisa says about electronic cigarettes
p: Anvisa, the Brazilian health regulator, published on 19 April 2024 (updated 14 June 2024) that it keeps the ban on electronic smoking devices. Importing them in any form is prohibited, including for personal use, and the page says bringing devices into the country is prohibited, including in hand luggage and in accompanied checked baggage. The ban covers manufacturing, importing, selling, distributing, storing, transporting and advertising, including accessories, parts and refills.

The rule does not ban individual use as such, but using these devices in enclosed collective spaces has been prohibited by law since 1996. Non-compliance is a sanitary infraction, and Anvisa lists possible warnings, closure, product seizure and fines under Laws 9.294/1996 and 6.437/1977, with referral to prosecutors possible. The page gives no fine amount, so treat any vape as an item not to pack for Brazil.
brazil.src: Source read: Anvisa, news item of 19 April 2024 (updated 14 June 2024), in Portuguese. No fine amount is stated.

hong-kong.h: What the Hong Kong Department of Health says about alternative smoking products
p: The Hong Kong government announced that from 30 April 2022 the Smoking (Public Health) (Amendment) Ordinance 2021 bans importing, promoting, manufacturing, selling and possessing alternative smoking products for commercial purposes. The products covered are e-cigarettes, heated tobacco products, herbal cigarettes and their accessories. Importing them by parcel, cargo or as an incoming traveller is prohibited, and travellers must declare all such products to Customs and Excise, whatever the quantity or personal use.

Some transit goods are exempt, such as items held in transit at Hong Kong International Airport without passing immigration, air transhipment cargo and items kept on an aircraft or vessel in transit. The maximum penalty is a fine of HK$50,000 and up to six months in prison, and smoking or carrying an activated product in a statutory no-smoking area carries a HK$1,500 fixed penalty notice. The Department of Health says these products contain nicotine at levels similar to cigarettes.
hong-kong.src: Source read: Hong Kong government press release of 28 April 2022 on the ban on alternative smoking products.

india.h: What the Indian Act of 2019 says about electronic cigarettes
p: The Indian Parliament's Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes (Production, Manufacture, Import, Export, Transport, Sale, Distribution, Storage and Advertisement) Act, 2019, Act No. 42 of 2019, deemed in force from 18 September 2019, says no person shall directly or indirectly produce, manufacture, import, export, transport, sell or distribute electronic cigarettes, whether as a complete product or any part of one. Import means bringing into India from a place outside India.

A person who breaks that rule is punishable with imprisonment of up to one year or a fine of up to one lakh rupees, or both, and for a second or later offence with up to three years in prison and a fine of up to five lakh rupees. The Act does not set a traveller allowance, so a vape in luggage is an import of an electronic cigarette. The Act is a legal text, not a customs guide, so ask Indian customs how it is enforced at the airport.
india.src: Source read: The Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019 (Gazette of India), published by the National Tobacco Control Programme.

mexico.h: What the Mexican customs agency says about e-cigarettes
p: The Mexican customs agency (ANAM) lists electronic cigarettes and similar electric or electronic personal vaporisers among the goods that cannot be brought into Mexico. The page says the scope explicitly covers newer products, including heated tobacco devices, electronic nicotine delivery systems, nicotine-free similar systems and alternative nicotine consumption systems, and cites tariff fraction 8543.40.01.
The page does not mention penalties. It lists other prohibited goods such as narcotics, weapons and ammunition. The separate ANAM luggage page we read says nothing about vapes, so leave them at home.
mexico.src: Source read: ANAM, Mercancía que no puedes ingresar a México (in Spanish). No penalty is stated.

singapore.h: What the Health Sciences Authority says about e-vaporisers at the border
p: The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) of Singapore reported that between 1 April and 30 June 2024 it ran joint operations with the immigration authority at Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints, Changi Airport, the cruise centres and the Tanah Merah ferry terminal. More than 5,000 travellers were checked and 19 were found with e-vaporisers. Travellers found with e-vaporisers or their components will be fined, and all prohibited tobacco items are seized and confiscated.

The page says possession, use or purchase carries a maximum fine of S$2,000 under the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act, and convicted foreigners will be deported and barred from re-entering. Importing, distributing or selling e-vaporisers is punishable by up to S$10,000 and or six months in prison for a first offence, and up to S$20,000 and or 12 months for a repeat offence. Transport companies and drivers who bring them in face enforcement action. The traveller fine amount is not stated.
singapore.src: Source read: HSA (Singapore), update on stepped-up enforcement against e-vaporisers (1 August 2024). The traveller fine amount is not stated.

sweden.h: What Swedish Customs says about e-cigarettes and refills
p: Tullverket says that to bring e-cigarettes and refills home to Sweden you must be 18 or older, the goods must be for your own private use, and you must carry them yourself. From another EU country you may bring up to 20 ml of nicotine-containing liquid duty- and tax-free. From outside the EU the duty-free limit is based on value: SEK 5,000 if you arrive by aircraft or commercial ferry, and SEK 3,500 by other means. Non-nicotine products from another EU country have no restrictions, and from outside the EU the same value limits apply.

The limits cover everything you bought on the trip, so SEK 3,000 of clothing leaves SEK 2,000 for e-liquid on an aircraft arrival. Above the limits, from outside the EU you pay customs duty and VAT, and from another EU country you pay VAT to the Swedish Tax Agency within 5 days. If you arrive from outside the EU with goods beyond the free allowances, you must declare them at the border. The page describes no fines.
sweden.src: Source read: Tullverket, Buying e-cigarettes and refills when travelling (English). No fines are stated.

united-arab-emirates.h: What the Dubai Customs restricted goods page says about e-cigarettes
p: The Dubai Customs page on prohibited and restricted goods lists e-cigarettes among restricted goods, grouped with new tyres and electronic hookahs, and names the Emirates Authority for Standardization and Metrology as the controlling authority. Restricted means the goods need approval from that authority before customs will release them, so a traveller cannot assume a device is allowed.

The same page lists other restricted items by authority, for example live animals and plants under the climate change and environment ministry, pharmaceuticals under the health ministry and alcoholic beverages under Dubai Police, and separately lists narcotic drugs among the prohibited items. It does not give a traveller allowance or a penalty for e-cigarettes.
united-arab-emirates.src: Source read: Dubai Customs, Prohibited and restricted goods. No allowance or penalty for e-cigarettes is stated.

mauritius.h: What the Mauritius Revenue Authority list shows for vapes
p: The Mauritius Revenue Authority document on selected prohibited goods lists tobacco-related items next to a quantity column, among them e-liquids and heated tobacco products as defined in the Public Health (Restrictions on Tobacco Products) Regulations 2022, and devices and accessories for use with ENDS, ENNDS and heated tobacco products.

As extracted text, the quantity column cannot be matched to each row with certainty, so we do not quote a figure for e-liquid or devices. Our card says vapes, e-liquid, accessories and heated tobacco are prohibited, which the list's heading supports. Ask the Mauritius Revenue Authority before you pack any device.
mauritius.src: Source read: MRA, Selected prohibited goods (PDF, extracted text). The quantity column could not be matched to rows.

argentina.h: Vapes in Argentina: the WHO profile and the general rule
p: Our card for Argentina comes from the WHO country profile, which describes how e-cigarettes are regulated for sale and use, not how many a traveller may carry.

No national customs page on vapes was available to read for Argentina, so this section applies the general rule: nicotine liquid is the part most often limited, in millilitres or in strength, while nicotine-free liquid is often treated more lightly. We have no published figure for Argentina, so ask the customs authority of Argentina.
argentina.src: No national customs page on vapes was read for Argentina; the WHO country profile on the card is the data. Global rule applied, unofficial.

canada.h: What the Canada Border Services Agency says about vaping products
p: The Canada Border Services Agency says non-residents and temporary residents must declare all tobacco and vaping products when they enter Canada, and the minimum age is 18 wherever you enter. For vaping products the limit is 12 vaping containers or fewer, with a maximum of 120 mL of liquid or 120 g of solid.

The page does not call vaping products within these limits duty-free. It says duties and taxes could apply to limited quantities and that you should be ready to pay them on any declared amount. Amounts above the limits may need a permit from the provincial or territorial authority, and vaping products cannot count as exempt gifts. It states no penalty for undeclared vaping products.
canada.src: Source read: CBSA, What can I bring: tobacco and vaping products for non-residents. No penalty for undeclared vaping products is stated.

fiji.h: What Fiji Revenue and Customs says about e-cigarettes
p: The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service lists e-cigarette liquid inside the tobacco allowance for travellers aged 18 or over: e-cigarettes are capped at 200 ml or 200 mg, next to 200 cigarettes or 200 g of cigars or tobacco. Chewing tobacco is prohibited. The goods must be carried by the traveller and not be for sale or for someone else.

Goods over the allowance, or intended for commercial use, are subject to duty. The page does not list tobacco or e-cigarettes as a separate trigger for ticking Yes on the arrival card, and it describes no penalty for e-cigarettes above 200 ml.
fiji.src: Source read: FRCS, Arriving in Fiji. No e-cigarette penalty is stated.

norway.h: What Norwegian Customs says about nicotine products and vapes
p: Norwegian Customs says unapproved new tobacco and nicotine products, such as nicotine pouches and heated tobacco, waterpipe tobacco and certain e-cigarettes, are not allowed to be brought in under the tobacco quota page. The quota itself is 200 cigarettes or 250 g of other tobacco for visitors from outside Norway.

The page does not name which e-cigarettes are covered, does not give a quantity for permitted ones, and describes no penalty. You may bring more than the quota only if you declare the excess, but that does not make a banned product legal. Check the Norwegian customs rules for the exact product before you pack a device or liquid.
norway.src: Source read: Toll.no, Alcohol and tobacco quotas (English). The list of banned e-cigarettes and any penalty are not on the page.

taiwan.h: What Taipei Customs says about e-cigarettes
p: Taipei Customs says e-cigarettes and e-liquids are prohibited, as are undeclared or unapproved designated tobacco products, and that carrying prohibited goods may lead to criminal penalties. Only government-approved designated tobacco products count within the 200-product duty-free allowance for passengers aged 20 or over.

For tobacco above the allowance the page gives fines and confiscation, for example NTD 1,000 per 200 cigarettes, and dutiable goods may be confiscated or fined up to three times their value. The page does not describe a specific penalty for a vape device, so treat it as an item not to pack.
taiwan.src: Source read: Customs Administration, Taipei Customs, duty-free page (English). A device-specific penalty is not stated.

serbia.h: What Serbian Customs says about vapes and nicotine pouches
p: Serbian Customs lists e-cigarettes, vapes, nicotine pouches and hookah flavours for personal use as allowed alongside the tobacco allowance of 50 cigarettes, 25 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of tobacco, and says snus is prohibited. The page gives no separate quantity for e-liquid or devices.

Goods up to EUR 3,000 can be cleared at the border in the red channel with a single 10% customs rate plus VAT, and the page states no minimum age for these products and no penalty. Because quantities are not stated, keep to amounts that are clearly for personal use.
serbia.src: Source read: Carina.rs, FAQ for tourists (English). No quantity, age rule or penalty for vapes is stated.

south-korea.h: What Korea Customs says about e-cigarette liquid
p: The Korea Customs Service page on duty-free allowances sets the tobacco allowance at 200 cigarette sticks, or e-cigarette or liquid nicotine up to 20 ml with nicotine under 1%. Minors under 19, counted by year of birth, are not given the tax exemption for liquor and cigarettes. The page does not mention cigars or loose tobacco.

If you declare goods above the allowances yourself, you get a 30% reduction from the standard customs duty. Undeclared goods found later face an additional tax of 40% above the regular tax, or 60% if caught two or more times within 2 years.
south-korea.src: Source read: Korea Customs Service, duty-free allowance page (English). The page does not say whether the 20 ml counts per device or in total.

georgia.h: What the Georgian Revenue Service brochure says about e-cigarette liquid
p: The Georgian Revenue Service customs brochure allows 50 ml of e-cigarette liquid, imported as hand luggage or baggage for personal or family use or as a gift, as one of the tobacco options: per 30 calendar days by road and per calendar day through air checkpoints. Heated tobacco products are counted as 200 pieces, and capsules with tobacco content as 10 pieces.

Combinations of tobacco products are allowed if the shares of each product, measured against its own limit, add up to no more than 100%. Tax benefits for tobacco and alcohol start at age 18. The brochure does not describe penalties for liquid above 50 ml.
georgia.src: Source read: Revenue Service of Georgia, brochure on exemption of goods from duties and declaring. It states no vape penalty.

qatar.h: What the UK government advice says about vapes in Qatar
p: We read the UK government's travel advice for Qatar. It says vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal to import and sell, including liquids and electronic shisha pipes, regardless of quantity and intended use, and that customs may confiscate them. It also says drugs are strictly controlled and that medicines should be checked with the Qatari embassy.

This is the advice of another country's government, which is why this is an unofficial source. The page gives no fine amount for vapes, but it says breaking the Qatari rules on money or goods can lead to a fine or imprisonment plus seizure.
qatar.src: Source read: UK government (FCDO), Qatar entry requirements, 16 November 2026. This is an unofficial source.

united-kingdom.h: What GOV.UK says about vaping products for Great Britain
p: GOV.UK says that for travellers aged 17 or under there are no personal allowances for alcohol, tobacco or vaping products; you can bring them for your own use but must declare them before arriving in Great Britain. Your goods could be seized if you do not declare them, and you declare online before travelling or at the border.

The page does not give a quantity limit for vaping products for adults, and the page covers Great Britain only, so check the separate guide for Northern Ireland. The tobacco allowance on the same page is one of 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars, 250 g of tobacco or 200 sticks for heated tobacco devices.
united-kingdom.src: Source read: GOV.UK, Duty-free goods: arriving in Great Britain. No adult quantity limit for vapes is stated.

thailand.h: What the Thai customs green channel page says about e-cigarettes
p: The Suvarnabhumi Airport customs page for the Nothing to Declare channel lists the allowance as up to 200 cigarettes, or 250 g of tobacco, or 250 g of all types combined, plus 1 litre of alcohol. It does not mention e-cigarettes or whether they are prohibited, so the page gives no basis to carry a vape.

Excess cigarettes, tobacco or alcohol must be put in the box provided by Customs, and the page warns that otherwise prosecution will be carried out. Prohibited or restricted goods lead to prosecution. Because Thailand treats vapes under its own rules, which this page does not cover, ask Thai Customs before you pack a device.
thailand.src: Source read: Thai Customs Department, Suvarnabhumi Airport green channel page. E-cigarettes are not covered on it.

japan.h: What Japan Customs says about tobacco and heated tobacco
p: Japan Customs lists the duty-free tobacco allowance per person over 20 as 200 cigarettes, or 50 cigars, or 10 packages of heat-not-burn tobacco, or 250 g of other tobacco products. The page applies the allowances only to people over 20 and says nothing about younger travellers, and it does not mention nicotine e-liquid.

An item worth more than 200,000 yen gets no allowance and is taxed in full. The page does not state the duty rates or the procedure for quantities above the allowance, so a nicotine vape device or liquid is not covered by what we read and should be checked with Japan Customs.
japan.src: Source read: Japan Customs, Customs Answer 7104 (English). Nicotine liquid is not covered on the page.

brazil.h: What Anvisa says about electronic cigarettes
p: Anvisa, the Brazilian health regulator, published on 19 April 2024 (updated 14 June 2024) that it keeps the ban on electronic smoking devices. Importing them in any form is prohibited, including for personal use, and the page says bringing devices into the country is prohibited, including in hand luggage and in accompanied checked baggage. The ban covers manufacturing, importing, selling, distributing, storing, transporting and advertising, including accessories, parts and refills.

The rule does not ban individual use as such, but using these devices in enclosed collective spaces has been prohibited by law since 1996. Non-compliance is a sanitary infraction, and Anvisa lists possible warnings, closure, product seizure and fines under Laws 9.294/1996 and 6.437/1977, with referral to prosecutors possible. The page gives no fine amount, so treat any vape as an item not to pack for Brazil.
brazil.src: Source read: Anvisa, news item of 19 April 2024 (updated 14 June 2024), in Portuguese. No fine amount is stated.

hong-kong.h: What the Hong Kong Department of Health says about alternative smoking products
p: The Hong Kong government announced that from 30 April 2022 the Smoking (Public Health) (Amendment) Ordinance 2021 bans importing, promoting, manufacturing, selling and possessing alternative smoking products for commercial purposes. The products covered are e-cigarettes, heated tobacco products, herbal cigarettes and their accessories. Importing them by parcel, cargo or as an incoming traveller is prohibited, and travellers must declare all such products to Customs and Excise, whatever the quantity or personal use.

Some transit goods are exempt, such as items held in transit at Hong Kong International Airport without passing immigration, air transhipment cargo and items kept on an aircraft or vessel in transit. The maximum penalty is a fine of HK$50,000 and up to six months in prison, and smoking or carrying an activated product in a statutory no-smoking area carries a HK$1,500 fixed penalty notice. The Department of Health says these products contain nicotine at levels similar to cigarettes.
hong-kong.src: Source read: Hong Kong government press release of 28 April 2022 on the ban on alternative smoking products.

india.h: What the Indian Act of 2019 says about electronic cigarettes
p: The Indian Parliament's Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes (Production, Manufacture, Import, Export, Transport, Sale, Distribution, Storage and Advertisement) Act, 2019, Act No. 42 of 2019, deemed in force from 18 September 2019, says no person shall directly or indirectly produce, manufacture, import, export, transport, sell or distribute electronic cigarettes, whether as a complete product or any part of one. Import means bringing into India from a place outside India.

A person who breaks that rule is punishable with imprisonment of up to one year or a fine of up to one lakh rupees, or both, and for a second or later offence with up to three years in prison and a fine of up to five lakh rupees. The Act does not set a traveller allowance, so a vape in luggage is an import of an electronic cigarette. The Act is a legal text, not a customs guide, so ask Indian customs how it is enforced at the airport.
india.src: Source read: The Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act, 2019 (Gazette of India), published by the National Tobacco Control Programme.

mexico.h: What the Mexican customs agency says about e-cigarettes
p: The Mexican customs agency (ANAM) lists electronic cigarettes and similar electric or electronic personal vaporisers among the goods that cannot be brought into Mexico. The page says the scope explicitly covers newer products, including heated tobacco devices, electronic nicotine delivery systems, nicotine-free similar systems and alternative nicotine consumption systems, and cites tariff fraction 8543.40.01.
The page does not mention penalties. It lists other prohibited goods such as narcotics, weapons and ammunition. The separate ANAM luggage page we read says nothing about vapes, so leave them at home.
mexico.src: Source read: ANAM, Mercancía que no puedes ingresar a México (in Spanish). No penalty is stated.

singapore.h: What the Health Sciences Authority says about e-vaporisers at the border
p: The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) of Singapore reported that between 1 April and 30 June 2024 it ran joint operations with the immigration authority at Woodlands and Tuas checkpoints, Changi Airport, the cruise centres and the Tanah Merah ferry terminal. More than 5,000 travellers were checked and 19 were found with e-vaporisers. Travellers found with e-vaporisers or their components will be fined, and all prohibited tobacco items are seized and confiscated.

The page says possession, use or purchase carries a maximum fine of S$2,000 under the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act, and convicted foreigners will be deported and barred from re-entering. Importing, distributing or selling e-vaporisers is punishable by up to S$10,000 and or six months in prison for a first offence, and up to S$20,000 and or 12 months for a repeat offence. Transport companies and drivers who bring them in face enforcement action. The traveller fine amount is not stated.
singapore.src: Source read: HSA (Singapore), update on stepped-up enforcement against e-vaporisers (1 August 2024). The traveller fine amount is not stated.

sweden.h: What Swedish Customs says about e-cigarettes and refills
p: Tullverket says that to bring e-cigarettes and refills home to Sweden you must be 18 or older, the goods must be for your own private use, and you must carry them yourself. From another EU country you may bring up to 20 ml of nicotine-containing liquid duty- and tax-free. From outside the EU the duty-free limit is based on value: SEK 5,000 if you arrive by aircraft or commercial ferry, and SEK 3,500 by other means. Non-nicotine products from another EU country have no restrictions, and from outside the EU the same value limits apply.

The limits cover everything you bought on the trip, so SEK 3,000 of clothing leaves SEK 2,000 for e-liquid on an aircraft arrival. Above the limits, from outside the EU you pay customs duty and VAT, and from another EU country you pay VAT to the Swedish Tax Agency within 5 days. If you arrive from outside the EU with goods beyond the free allowances, you must declare them at the border. The page describes no fines.
sweden.src: Source read: Tullverket, Buying e-cigarettes and refills when travelling (English). No fines are stated.

united-arab-emirates.h: What the Dubai Customs restricted goods page says about e-cigarettes
p: The Dubai Customs page on prohibited and restricted goods lists e-cigarettes among restricted goods, grouped with new tyres and electronic hookahs, and names the Emirates Authority for Standardization and Metrology as the controlling authority. Restricted means the goods need approval from that authority before customs will release them, so a traveller cannot assume a device is allowed.

The same page lists other restricted items by authority, for example live animals and plants under the climate change and environment ministry, pharmaceuticals under the health ministry and alcoholic beverages under Dubai Police, and separately lists narcotic drugs among the prohibited items. It does not give a traveller allowance or a penalty for e-cigarettes.
united-arab-emirates.src: Source read: Dubai Customs, Prohibited and restricted goods. No allowance or penalty for e-cigarettes is stated.

mauritius.h: What the Mauritius Revenue Authority list shows for vapes
p: The Mauritius Revenue Authority document on selected prohibited goods lists tobacco-related items next to a quantity column, among them e-liquids and heated tobacco products as defined in the Public Health (Restrictions on Tobacco Products) Regulations 2022, and devices and accessories for use with ENDS, ENNDS and heated tobacco products.

As extracted text, the quantity column cannot be matched to each row with certainty, so we do not quote a figure for e-liquid or devices. Our card says vapes, e-liquid, accessories and heated tobacco are prohibited, which the list's heading supports. Ask the Mauritius Revenue Authority before you pack any device.
mauritius.src: Source read: MRA, Selected prohibited goods (PDF, extracted text). The quantity column could not be matched to rows.

costa-rica.h: Vapes in Costa Rica: Law 10066 and the 2024 import ban
p: The WHO FCTC secretariat records Costa Rica's Law No. 10066, in force since 20 January 2022. It covers nicotine and non-nicotine e-cigarettes and heated tobacco, bans their use wherever smoking is banned (with signs and fines), bans selling them to under-18s, and adds a 20% excise tax on devices, accessories and liquids, local or imported, charged on the import (CIF) value.

La Nación reported on 14 May 2024 that the Ministry of Health published a resolution in the official gazette banning the import, use and sale of products with synthetic nicotine while a technical regulation is drawn up. The article was behind a paywall, so we read only its headline and summary: a traveller carrying such a product could face confiscation, so ask the Ministry of Health or Costa Rican customs before packing any device or liquid. No customs page on traveller quantities was readable.
costa-rica.src: Source read 23 November 2026: WHO FCTC implementation database, "Costa Rica regulates the use and taxation on ENDS, ENNDS and HTPs" (24 January 2022), and La Nación (nacion.com), 14 May 2024 (headline and summary only). Both are unofficial for Costa Rica; its customs and Ministry of Health sites refused our reader.
link: WHO FCTC: Costa Rica Law 10066 on ENDS, ENNDS and heated tobacco

lithuania.h: What Lithuanian Customs says about vapes and heated tobacco
p: Lithuanian Customs gives a duty-free allowance for e-cigarette liquid and heated tobacco to travellers over 17 arriving from outside the EU. By air: 50 ml of e-cigarette liquid and 200 heated-tobacco units. By any other transport (road, rail, sea), and for crew and border-zone residents: 20 ml of e-cigarette liquid and 40 heated-tobacco units. These sit beside the cigarette allowance and are counted separately.

The Lithuanian drug, tobacco and alcohol control department adds that the law treats nicotine-free liquid as an e-cigarette liquid too, and that flavoured liquids other than tobacco flavour may not be placed on the Lithuanian market since 1 July 2022, so a flavoured refill is a risk at the border even though it is for personal use. Imports of cigarettes and tobacco from Russia and Belarus are banned.
lithuania.src: Official source read 23 November 2026: Lithuanian Customs (Lietuvos Respublikos muitine), "Coming from third countries" (muitine.lrv.lt, English; read from an archived copy because the live site refuses our reader). EU-travel figures from Hinterland Travel (unofficial, read 23 November 2026). Flavour ban: Narkotikų, tabako ir alkoholio kontrolės departamentas, "Electronic cigarettes and their refill containers" (ntakd.lrv.lt, archived copy).
link: Lithuanian Customs: coming from third countries
